[[伊勢神宮]]{{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮}}（外宮）の別宮。社殿は外宮に準じ[[千木・鰹木|外削ぎの千木と、5本で奇数の鰹木]]を持つ萱葺の[[神明造]]で南面している。遷宮のための古殿地は東西に隣接している。外宮に準じ、20年に一度[[Jingū Shikinen Sengū|遷宮]]が行われる。その昔、月夜見宮の所在地の宮後町の民が役木を曳いて八日市場町にさしかかったときに宮後町で火事が起き、曳き手が消火のため帰ってしまったので、八日市場町の民が代わって役木を曳き、それ以来'''[[御木曳|御木曳初式]]'''（おきひきぞめしき）では八日市場町の民が月夜見宮に役木を奉曳することになったとの伝承がある。 * {{ill|Takagawara Shrine|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} - 祭神：月夜見尊御魂（つきよみのみことのみたま）。月夜見宮の境内にあるが伊勢神宮豊受大神宮（外宮）の[[摂社]]である。 * [[稲荷社]] * 宿衛屋 == 神路通り == [[File:Kamiji Street from Tsukiyomi no Miya.jpg|thumb|神路通り]] 外宮の北御門（きたみかど）から月夜見宮までの、幅員4m程度の1直線の道は「神が通る道」とされ、「'''神路通り'''（かみじどおり）」と呼ばれる。[[神路通り]]の項目を参照。 == 信者団体 == [[1960年]]（昭和35年）に伊勢市在住の崇敬者を中心に月夜見講が発足され、のちに月夜見宮奉賛会と改称した。月夜見宮奉賛会は毎年4月と9月の19日に神恩感謝の祭を行うなどの活動をしている。 == 交通 == * [[東海旅客鉄道|JR]][[参宮線]]・[[近畿日本鉄道|近鉄]][[近鉄山田線|山田線]][[伊勢市駅]]から徒歩約10分。 * 外宮北御門口から[[神路通り]]経由で徒歩約5分JTBパブリッシング（2011）：43ページ。 * [[三重交通]]新道バス停下車徒歩約3分、[[伊勢市コミュニティバス|伊勢市コミュニティバス「おかげバス」]]月夜見宮前バス停下車すぐ2013年7月20日から運行が開始された三重交通の「参宮バス」が「月夜見宮前」停留所に停車していたが、2015年3月31日をもって「月夜見宮前」停留所への乗り入れが廃止された。 * [[伊勢自動車道]][[伊勢インターチェンジ]]から約3km * 駐車場：鳥居前には2-4台しか駐車できないが、南面する道路に[[駐車場|パーキングメーター]]がある。 == 脚注 == {{Reflist}} == 参考文献 == * 『月夜見宮参拝のしおり』（発行：神宮司庁） * 『お伊勢さんを歩こう』（発行：伊勢神宮崇敬会） * 『お伊勢まいり』（発行：伊勢神宮崇敬会） * 『宇治山田市史』 * 金子延夫『玉城町史 二巻 －南伊勢の歴史と伝承－』三重県郷土資料叢書第91集、三重県郷土資料刊行会、昭和58年12月10日 * 出版事業本部 国内情報部 第三編集部 編『[[るるぶ]] お伊勢まいり』るるぶ情報版近畿21、通巻4615号、[[JTBパブリッシング]]、2014年5月1日、92p. ISBN 978-4-533-09761-4 * [[三橋健 (神道学者)|三橋健]]『伊勢神宮 日本人は何を祈ってきたのか』[[朝日新書]]416、[[朝日新聞出版]]、2013年8月30日、230p. ISBN 978-4-02-273516-4 * 矢野憲一『伊勢神宮―知られざる杜のうち』角川選書402、[[角川学芸出版]]、平成18年11月10日、270p. ISBN 4-04-703402-9 * 『伊勢神宮』楽学ブックス 神社1、JTBパブリッシング、2011年4月1日、143p. ISBN 978-4-533-08206-1 * 『日本人なら知っておきたい 伊勢神宮と125の社』タツミムック、[[辰巳出版]]、2013年11月1日、127p. ISBN 978-4-7778-1197-7 * 『いま行く!伊勢神宮お参りパーフェクトブック』みらい出版、2013年12月10日、107p. {{distinguish|{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|2=es|3=Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|4=ja|5=月讀宮|lkt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya}}}} {{混同|月讀宮|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|2=es|3=Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|4=ja|5=月讀宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya}} {{神社 | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Geku Tsukiyomi no Miya in October 2016.jpg|270px]]
社殿 |名称 = 月夜見宮 |所在地 = [[三重県]][[伊勢市]]宮後一丁目3-19 |位置 = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|29|34.7|N|136|42|21.3|E|display=inline,title}} |祭神 = [[ツクヨミ|月夜見尊]]
月夜見尊荒御魂 |社格 = [[式内社]]（小）
{{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮}}別宮 |創建 = [[延長 (元号)|延長]]5年（[[927年]]）以前 |本殿 = [[神明造]] |例祭= |地図 = {{location map|Japan Mie|lat_deg=34|lat_min=29|lat_sec=34.7|lon_deg=136|lon_min=42|lon_sec=21.3|label=月夜見宮|position=top|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|34|29|34.7|N|136|42|21.3|E}}}} }} '''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya''' (月夜見宮) is a [[Shinto shrine|shrine]] located in Miyago, Ise City, Mie Prefecture辰巳出版（2013）：16ページ. It is a [[Betsugū]] of [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]] {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮}} (Outer Shrine)伊勢文化舎 編（2008）：39ページみらい出版（2013）：64ページ学研パブリッシング（2013）：69ページJTBパブリッシング（2011）：42ページ出版事業本部 国内情報部 第三編集部 編（2014）：34ページ三橋（2013）：124ページ。 It is a [[Shikinaisha]]. == Overview == [[File:Tsukiyomi-nomiya(Geku)_00.JPG|thumb|300px|right|Aerial view of Tsukiyomi-no-Miya]] Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is an auxiliary shrine (betsugu) of the Outer Shrine (Geku), located about 300 meters north of Geku and approximately 500 meters west of {{ill|Ise City Station|ja|伊勢市駅}}. It enshrines two deities within the same shrine building: {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto|ja|月夜見尊}} (Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto) and his fierce spirit, **Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto-no-Aramitama** (荒御魂 of Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto) . Unlike the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya}} auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine (Naiku), where Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto and his Aramitama are enshrined separately, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya uniquely houses both deities within a single structure . The only other auxiliary shrines that enshrine two deities in one building are {{ill|Kaze-no-Miya|ja|風宮}} (Kaze-no-Miya) of the Outer Shrine and {{ill|Kazahinomi-no-Miya|ja|風日祈宮|lt=Kazahi-no-Miya}} of the Inner Shrine, both enshrining Shinatsuhiko-no-Mikoto (級長津彦命) and Shinatsuhime-no-Mikoto (級長戸辺命). Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is the only auxiliary shrine of the Outer Shrine located outside the main precincts . Despite being in the urban area of Ise City, its grounds maintain a serene atmosphere . The moat surrounding three sides of the precinct is thought to be a remnant of a tributary of the {{ill|Miyagawa River (Mie Prefecture)|ja|宮川 (三重県)}} . The {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 37|ja|三重県道37号鳥羽松阪線}} runs along the northern side of the moat and serves as the route for the **Hatsuhobiki** (初穂曳), a festival procession held every October in conjunction with the {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}. During this event, decorated carts carry the first harvested rice offerings to the Outer Shrine. Adjacent to the right rear of the shrine building is the auxiliary shrine of {{ill|Takagawara Shrine|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} . To the left rear stands an {{ill|Inari shrine|ja|稲荷}} , and to the right is a large sacred camphor tree (大楠), where many people offer prayers . Like other auxiliary shrines outside the main precincts, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya has a **Shukueiya** (宿衛屋), a guardhouse where Shinto priests are present during visiting hours to distribute amulets, offer kagura performances, and manage food offerings (御饌). == Worshipped Deities (Saijin) == {{see also|{{ill|Saijin|ja|祭神}}}} * {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|ja|ツクヨミ}}（つきよみのみこと） * {{nihongo|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto-no-Ara-Mitama|月夜見尊荒御魂}} : {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|ja|月夜見尊}} is the same deity as {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|ja|月讀尊}}, the enshrined deity of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月讀宮}}, an auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine (Naikū) of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮}}. He is the brother of {{ill|Amaterasu Ōmikami|ja|天照大神}}. Since agricultural activities historically relied on the lunar calendar ({{ill|Lunisolar calendar|ja|太陰暦}}), he has been worshipped as a deity of agriculture. Additionally, he is also considered a river deity of {{ill|Takagawara|ja|高河原}} and a deity associated with women. According to the *{{ill|Jinmyō Hisho|ja|神名秘書}}*, his {{ill|Shintai|ja|神体}} (sacred object) is a {{ill|mirror|ja|鏡}}. == Festivals == The shrine follows a festival schedule similar to that of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮}}, with offerings from the {{ill|Imperial House of Japan|ja|皇室}} during prayers for the harvest (*{{ill|Kinensai|ja|祈年祭}}*), seasonal festivals (*{{ill|Tsukinamisai|ja|月次祭}}*), and major thanksgiving ceremonies (*{{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}* and *{{ill|Niinamesai|ja|新嘗祭}}*). * **January** * *{{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭}}* (New Year's Festival) – {{ill|January 1|ja|1月1日}} * A festival celebrating the new year and praying for the eternal prosperity of the imperial lineage. * *{{ill|Genshi-sai|ja|元始祭}}* (Imperial Foundation Festival) – {{ill|January 3|ja|1月3日}} * A festival celebrating the origins of the imperial rule. * **February** * *{{ill|Kenkoku Kinen-sai|ja|建国記念祭}}* (National Foundation Festival) – {{ill|February 11|ja|2月11日}} * Celebrating the founding of Japan by {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|ja|神武天皇}}. * *{{ill|Kinensai|ja|祈年祭}}* (Prayer Festival) – {{ill|February 18|ja|2月18日}} * A ceremony held early in the year to pray for abundant grain harvests and national peace. * *{{ill|Tenchō-sai|ja|天長祭}}* (Emperor’s Birthday Festival) – {{ill|February 23|ja|2月23日}} * A festival honoring the birthday of {{ill|Emperor Naruhito|ja|徳仁天皇}}. * **May** * *{{ill|Kazahinomi-sai|ja|風日祈祭}}* (Wind and Sun Festival) – {{ill|May 14|ja|5月14日}} * Offerings are made at the Outer Shrine, Inner Shrine, and affiliated shrines to pray for protection from storms and a bountiful harvest. * **June** * *{{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭}}* (Monthly Festival) – {{ill|June 18|ja|6月18日}}–{{ill|June 19|ja|6月19日}} * A biannual festival held in June and December to pray for the well-being of the nation and the emperor. Together with *{{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}*, these are called the *Three Great Festivals* (三節祭 or 三時祭). * **August** * *{{ill|Kazahinomi-sai|ja|風日祈祭}}* (Wind and Sun Festival) – {{ill|August 4|ja|8月4日}} * A repetition of the May festival to pray for good weather and agricultural prosperity. * **October** * *{{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}* (First Fruits Festival) – {{ill|October 18|ja|10月18日}}–{{ill|October 19|ja|10月19日}} * A festival where priests present freshly harvested grains as offerings to the gods. * **November** * *{{ill|Niinamesai|ja|新嘗祭}}* (New Harvest Festival) – {{ill|November 24|ja|11月24日}} * A festival in which the emperor offers the season’s first grains to the gods and partakes in them as an act of gratitude. * **December** * *{{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭}}* (Monthly Festival) – {{ill|December 18|ja|12月18日}}–{{ill|December 19|ja|12月19日}} === {{ill|Shikinen Sengu|ja|式年遷宮}} === [[File:Sengu of Tsukiyomi no Miya, August 2014.jpg|thumb|{{ill|Ritchūsai|ja|立柱祭}}を控えた{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮}}（2014年8月11日撮影）
左側が当時の社殿、右側が建設中の社殿]] {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮}}の第62回{{ill|Shikinen Sengu|ja|式年遷宮}}の諸祭と日程は以下の通りである{{Cite web|和書|url=http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2259/|title=伊勢神宮外宮別宮のもう一つの「月の神様」もお引っ越し―残すは風宮|publisher=[[伊勢志摩経済新聞]]|date=2015-03-03|accessdate=2015-03-07|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150307142246/http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2259/|archivedate=2015-03-07}}{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.isejingu.or.jp/sikinen_2.html|title=月讀宮以下12別宮の遷宮 - 伊勢神宮|publisher=神宮司庁|accessdate=2015-03-07|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150210061619/http://www.isejingu.or.jp/sikinen_2.html|archivedate=2015-02-10}}。 **2014年** * {{ill|August 20|ja|8月20日}} - {{ill|Ritchūsai|ja|立柱祭}}（りっちゅうさい）・{{ill|Jōtōsai|ja|上棟祭}}（じょうとうさい） * {{ill|October 5|ja|10月5日}} - {{ill|Nokitsukesai|ja|檐付祭}}（のきつけさい） * {{ill|November 5|ja|11月5日}} - {{ill|Irakasai|ja|甍祭}}（いらかさい） **2015年** * {{ill|February 26|ja|2月26日}} - {{ill|Mitosai|ja|御戸祭}}（みとさい）・{{ill|Mifunashiro Hōnō-shiki|ja|御船代奉納式}}（みふなしろほうのうしき）・{{ill|Araikiyome|ja|洗清}}（あらいきよめ） * {{ill|February 27|ja|2月27日}} - {{ill|Kotsukisai|ja|杵築祭}}（こつきさい）・{{ill|Gochinsai|ja|後鎮祭}}（ごちんさい）・{{ill|Kawahara Ōharai|ja|川原大祓}}（かわらおおはらい） * {{ill|February 28|ja|2月28日}} - {{ill|Okazari|ja|御飾}}（おかざり）・{{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御}}（せんぎょ） * {{ill|March 1|ja|3月1日}} - {{ill|Ōmike|ja|大御饌}}（おおみけ）・{{ill|Hōhei|ja|奉幣}} Above, the {{ill|Ritchūsai|ja|立柱祭}}, {{ill|Jōtōsai|ja|上棟祭}}, {{ill|Kotsukisai|ja|杵築祭}}, {{ill|Gochinsai|ja|後鎮祭}}, {{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御}}, and {{ill|Hōhei|ja|奉幣}} were scheduled according to the divine decision (*{{ill|Gojijō|ja|御治定}}*) of the reigning emperor。 Additionally, on {{ill|February 22|ja|2月22日}}, the *{{ill|Oshiraishi-mochi|ja|お白石持}}* ceremony took place, during which approximately 1,000 participants from the {{ill|Miyago Hōkendan|ja|宮後奉献団}} carried sacred stones (*{{ill|Oshiraishi|ja|御白石}}*) in a cart from the {{ill|Urakuchi Intersection|ja|浦口交差点}} to {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮}}, covering a distance of 1.2 km{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.chunichi.co.jp/article/mie/20150223/CK2015022302000028.html|title=次代につなぐ「エンヤ」 伊勢・月夜見宮でお白石持行事|author=中平雄大|publisher=[[中日新聞]]|date=2015-02-23|accessdate=2015-03-08|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150307161058/http://www.chunichi.co.jp/article/mie/20150223/CK2015022302000028.html|archivedate=2015-03-07}}。 This marked the completion of the *Oshiraishi-mochi* ceremonies for all auxiliary shrines (*{{ill|Betsugū|ja|別宮}}*)。 == 境内 == * 月夜見宮 - [[伊勢神宮]]{{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮}}（外宮）の別宮。社殿は外宮に準じ[[千木・鰹木|外削ぎの千木と、5本で奇数の鰹木]]を持つ萱葺の[[神明造]]で南面している。遷宮のための古殿地は東西に隣接している。外宮に準じ、20年に一度[[Jingū Shikinen Sengū|遷宮]]が行われる。その昔、月夜見宮の所在地の宮後町の民が役木を曳いて八日市場町にさしかかったときに宮後町で火事が起き、曳き手が消火のため帰ってしまったので、八日市場町の民が代わって役木を曳き、それ以来'''[[御木曳|御木曳初式]]'''（おきひきぞめしき）では八日市場町の民が月夜見宮に役木を奉曳することになったとの伝承がある。 * {{ill|Takagawara Shrine|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} - 祭神：月夜見尊御魂（つきよみのみことのみたま）。月夜見宮の境内にあるが伊勢神宮豊受大神宮（外宮）の[[摂社]]である。 * [[稲荷社]] * 宿衛屋 == 神路通り == [[File:Kamiji Street from Tsukiyomi no Miya.jpg|thumb|神路通り]] 外宮の北御門（きたみかど）から月夜見宮までの、幅員4m程度の1直線の道は「神が通る道」とされ、「'''神路通り'''（かみじどおり）」と呼ばれる。[[神路通り]]の項目を参照。 == 信者団体 == [[1960年]]（昭和35年）に伊勢市在住の崇敬者を中心に月夜見講が発足され、のちに月夜見宮奉賛会と改称した。月夜見宮奉賛会は毎年4月と9月の19日に神恩感謝の祭を行うなどの活動をしている。 == 交通 == * [[東海旅客鉄道|JR]][[参宮線]]・[[近畿日本鉄道|近鉄]][[近鉄山田線|山田線]][[伊勢市駅]]から徒歩約10分。 * 外宮北御門口から[[神路通り]]経由で徒歩約5分JTBパブリッシング（2011）：43ページ。 * [[三重交通]]新道バス停下車徒歩約3分、[[伊勢市コミュニティバス|伊勢市コミュニティバス「おかげバス」]]月夜見宮前バス停下車すぐ2013年7月20日から運行が開始された三重交通の「参宮バス」が「月夜見宮前」停留所に停車していたが、2015年3月31日をもって「月夜見宮前」停留所への乗り入れが廃止された。 * [[伊勢自動車道]][[伊勢インターチェンジ]]から約3km * 駐車場：鳥居前には2-4台しか駐車できないが、南面する道路に[[駐車場|パーキングメーター]]がある。 == 脚注 == {{Reflist}} == 参考文献 == * 『月夜見宮参拝のしおり』（発行：神宮司庁） * 『お伊勢さんを歩こう』（発行：伊勢神宮崇敬会） * 『お伊勢まいり』（発行：伊勢神宮崇敬会） * 『宇治山田市史』 * 金子延夫『玉城町史 二巻 －南伊勢の歴史と伝承－』三重県郷土資料叢書第91集、三重県郷土資料刊行会、昭和58年12月10日 * 出版事業本部 国内情報部 第三編集部 編『[[るるぶ]] お伊勢まいり』るるぶ情報版近畿21、通巻4615号、[[JTBパブリッシング]]、2014年5月1日、92p. ISBN 978-4-533-09761-4 * [[三橋健 (神道学者)|三橋健]]『伊勢神宮 日本人は何を祈ってきたのか』[[朝日新書]]416、[[朝日新聞出版]]、2013年8月30日、230p. ISBN 978-4-02-273516-4 * 矢野憲一『伊勢神宮―知られざる杜のうち』角川選書402、[[角川学芸出版]]、平成18年11月10日、270p. ISBN 4-04-703402-9 * 『伊勢神宮』楽学ブックス 神社1、JTBパブリッシング、2011年4月1日、143p. ISBN 978-4-533-08206-1 * 『日本人なら知っておきたい 伊勢神宮と125の社』タツミムック、[[辰巳出版]]、2013年11月1日、127p. ISBN 978-4-7778-1197-7 * 『いま行く!伊勢神宮お参りパーフェクトブック』みらい出版、2013年12月10日、107p. ISBN 978-4-907292-14-0 == See Also == * [[ツクヨミ]] * [[伊勢国の式内社一覧]] * {{ill|List of 125 Shrines of Ise|ja|神宮125社の一覧}} * [[神路通り]] == 外部リンク == {{commonscat|Tsukiyomi-no-miya (Geku)}} * [http://www.isejingu.or.jp/about/geku/tsukiyomi.html 月夜見宮] - 伊勢神宮公式サイト * [http://www.jingukaikan.jp/125mairi/m02/0202.html 月夜見宮（つきよみのみや） - 神宮会館] - 一般財団法人伊勢神宮崇敬会 * [http://www.ise-kanko.jp/base_data/base_data.php?info_cd=00269 伊勢市観光協会/月夜見宮] * [http://www.barifuri.com/tourcenter/data_kankou/tsukiyomi_1/index.html 月夜見宮（つきよみのみや）] - 伊勢志摩バリアフリーツアーセンター {{125 Shrines of Ise}} {{神道 横}} {{125 Shrines of Ise|つきよみのみや}} [[Category:125 Shrines of Ise]] [[Category:Completion tier 3]][[Category:tier 3]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)]] [[Category:Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)]][[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:Tsukiyominomiya]][[ja:月夜見宮]][[Category:Tsukiyominomiya]][[Category:伊勢国の式内社]] [[Category:伊勢市の神社]] [[Category:2015年竣工の日本の建築物]] [[Category:refreshing imported pages]][[Category:refreshing imported pages]] [[Category:category refresh]] [[Category:pgoodbye $1]][[Category:new pages]][[Category:Tsukiyominomiya]][[Category:pgoodbye $1]][[Category:new pages]] [[Category:fixing the kk issue]] [[Category:Tsukiyomi-no-Miya]] [[Category:U]][[Category: pages]] [[Category:Sqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqq]] [[Category:qqqq]] [[Category:q--q]] [[Category:qq]] [[Category:trimming off this bad category]][[sn:Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)]][[Category:trimming off this bad category]] [[en:Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)]] [[Category:New]]

{{distinguish|{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|2=es|3=Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|4=ja|5=月讀宮|lkt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya}}}} {{混同|月讀宮|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|2=es|3=Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|4=ja|5=月讀宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya}} {{神社 | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Geku Tsukiyomi no Miya in October 2016.jpg|270px]]
社殿 |名称 = 月夜見宮 |所在地 = [[三重県]][[伊勢市]]宮後一丁目3-19 |位置 = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|29|34.7|N|136|42|21.3|E|display=inline,title}} |祭神 = [[ツクヨミ|月夜見尊]]
月夜見尊荒御魂 |社格 = [[式内社]]（小）
{{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮}}別宮 |創建 = [[延長 (元号)|延長]]5年（[[927年]]）以前 |本殿 = [[神明造]] |例祭= |地図 = {{location map|Japan Mie|lat_deg=34|lat_min=29|lat_sec=34.7|lon_deg=136|lon_min=42|lon_sec=21.3|label=月夜見宮|position=top|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|34|29|34.7|N|136|42|21.3|E}}}} }} '''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya''' (月夜見宮) is a [[Shinto shrine|shrine]] located in Miyago, Ise City, Mie Prefecture辰巳出版（2013）：16ページ. It is a [[Betsugū]] of [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]] {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮}} (Outer Shrine)伊勢文化舎 編（2008）：39ページみらい出版（2013）：64ページ学研パブリッシング（2013）：69ページJTBパブリッシング（2011）：42ページ出版事業本部 国内情報部 第三編集部 編（2014）：34ページ三橋（2013）：124ページ。 It is a [[Shikinaisha]]. == Overview == [[File:Tsukiyomi-nomiya(Geku)_00.JPG|thumb|300px|right|Aerial view of Tsukiyomi-no-Miya]] Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is an auxiliary shrine (betsugu) of the Outer Shrine (Geku), located about 300 meters north of Geku and approximately 500 meters west of {{ill|Ise City Station|ja|伊勢市駅}}. It enshrines two deities within the same shrine building: {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto|ja|月夜見尊}} (Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto) and his fierce spirit, **Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto-no-Aramitama** (荒御魂 of Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto) . Unlike the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya}} auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine (Naiku), where Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto and his Aramitama are enshrined separately, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya uniquely houses both deities within a single structure . The only other auxiliary shrines that enshrine two deities in one building are {{ill|Kaze-no-Miya|ja|風宮}} (Kaze-no-Miya) of the Outer Shrine and {{ill|Kazahinomi-no-Miya|ja|風日祈宮|lt=Kazahi-no-Miya}} of the Inner Shrine, both enshrining Shinatsuhiko-no-Mikoto (級長津彦命) and Shinatsuhime-no-Mikoto (級長戸辺命). Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is the only auxiliary shrine of the Outer Shrine located outside the main precincts . Despite being in the urban area of Ise City, its grounds maintain a serene atmosphere . The moat surrounding three sides of the precinct is thought to be a remnant of a tributary of the {{ill|Miyagawa River (Mie Prefecture)|ja|宮川 (三重県)}} . The {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 37|ja|三重県道37号鳥羽松阪線}} runs along the northern side of the moat and serves as the route for the **Hatsuhobiki** (初穂曳), a festival procession held every October in conjunction with the {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}. During this event, decorated carts carry the first harvested rice offerings to the Outer Shrine. Adjacent to the right rear of the shrine building is the auxiliary shrine of {{ill|Takagawara Shrine|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} . To the left rear stands an {{ill|Inari shrine|ja|稲荷}} , and to the right is a large sacred camphor tree (大楠), where many people offer prayers . Like other auxiliary shrines outside the main precincts, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya has a **Shukueiya** (宿衛屋), a guardhouse where Shinto priests are present during visiting hours to distribute amulets, offer kagura performances, and manage food offerings (御饌). == Worshipped Deities (Saijin) == {{see also|{{ill|Saijin|ja|祭神}}}} * {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|ja|ツクヨミ}}（つきよみのみこと） * {{nihongo|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto-no-Ara-Mitama|月夜見尊荒御魂}} : {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|ja|月夜見尊}} is the same deity as {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|ja|月讀尊}}, the enshrined deity of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月讀宮}}, an auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine (Naikū) of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮}}. He is the brother of {{ill|Amaterasu Ōmikami|ja|天照大神}}. Since agricultural activities historically relied on the lunar calendar ({{ill|Lunisolar calendar|ja|太陰暦}}), he has been worshipped as a deity of agriculture. Additionally, he is also considered a river deity of {{ill|Takagawara|ja|高河原}} and a deity associated with women. According to the *{{ill|Jinmyō Hisho|ja|神名秘書}}*, his {{ill|Shintai|ja|神体}} (sacred object) is a {{ill|mirror|ja|鏡}}. == Festivals == The shrine follows a festival schedule similar to that of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮}}, with offerings from the {{ill|Imperial House of Japan|ja|皇室}} during prayers for the harvest (*{{ill|Kinensai|ja|祈年祭}}*), seasonal festivals (*{{ill|Tsukinamisai|ja|月次祭}}*), and major thanksgiving ceremonies (*{{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}* and *{{ill|Niinamesai|ja|新嘗祭}}*). * **January** * *{{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭}}* (New Year's Festival) – {{ill|January 1|ja|1月1日}} * A festival celebrating the new year and praying for the eternal prosperity of the imperial lineage. * *{{ill|Genshi-sai|ja|元始祭}}* (Imperial Foundation Festival) – {{ill|January 3|ja|1月3日}} * A festival celebrating the origins of the imperial rule. * **February** * *{{ill|Kenkoku Kinen-sai|ja|建国記念祭}}* (National Foundation Festival) – {{ill|February 11|ja|2月11日}} * Celebrating the founding of Japan by {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|ja|神武天皇}}. * *{{ill|Kinensai|ja|祈年祭}}* (Prayer Festival) – {{ill|February 18|ja|2月18日}} * A ceremony held early in the year to pray for abundant grain harvests and national peace. * *{{ill|Tenchō-sai|ja|天長祭}}* (Emperor’s Birthday Festival) – {{ill|February 23|ja|2月23日}} * A festival honoring the birthday of {{ill|Emperor Naruhito|ja|徳仁天皇}}. * **May** * *{{ill|Kazahinomi-sai|ja|風日祈祭}}* (Wind and Sun Festival) – {{ill|May 14|ja|5月14日}} * Offerings are made at the Outer Shrine, Inner Shrine, and affiliated shrines to pray for protection from storms and a bountiful harvest. * **June** * *{{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭}}* (Monthly Festival) – {{ill|June 18|ja|6月18日}}–{{ill|June 19|ja|6月19日}} * A biannual festival held in June and December to pray for the well-being of the nation and the emperor. Together with *{{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}*, these are called the *Three Great Festivals* (三節祭 or 三時祭). * **August** * *{{ill|Kazahinomi-sai|ja|風日祈祭}}* (Wind and Sun Festival) – {{ill|August 4|ja|8月4日}} * A repetition of the May festival to pray for good weather and agricultural prosperity. * **October** * *{{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}* (First Fruits Festival) – {{ill|October 18|ja|10月18日}}–{{ill|October 19|ja|10月19日}} * A festival where priests present freshly harvested grains as offerings to the gods. * **November** * *{{ill|Niinamesai|ja|新嘗祭}}* (New Harvest Festival) – {{ill|November 24|ja|11月24日}} * A festival in which the emperor offers the season’s first grains to the gods and partakes in them as an act of gratitude. * **December** * *{{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭}}* (Monthly Festival) – {{ill|December 18|ja|12月18日}}–{{ill|December 19|ja|12月19日}} === {{ill|Shikinen Sengu|ja|式年遷宮}} === [[File:Sengu of Tsukiyomi no Miya, August 2014.jpg|thumb|{{ill|Ritchūsai|ja|立柱祭}}を控えた{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮}}（2014年8月11日撮影）
左側が当時の社殿、右側が建設中の社殿]] {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮}}の第62回{{ill|Shikinen Sengu|ja|式年遷宮}}の諸祭と日程は以下の通りである{{Cite web|和書|url=http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2259/|title=伊勢神宮外宮別宮のもう一つの「月の神様」もお引っ越し―残すは風宮|publisher=[[伊勢志摩経済新聞]]|date=2015-03-03|accessdate=2015-03-07|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150307142246/http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2259/|archivedate=2015-03-07}}{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.isejingu.or.jp/sikinen_2.html|title=月讀宮以下12別宮の遷宮 - 伊勢神宮|publisher=神宮司庁|accessdate=2015-03-07|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150210061619/http://www.isejingu.or.jp/sikinen_2.html|archivedate=2015-02-10}}。 The festivals and dates of the 62nd annual {{ill|Shikinen Sengu|ja|式年遷宮}} of the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮}} are as follows ==== 2014 ==== * {{ill|August 20|ja|8月20日}} - {{ill|Ritchūsai|ja|立柱祭}}（りっちゅうさい）・{{ill|Jōtōsai|ja|上棟祭}}（じょうとうさい） * {{ill|October 5|ja|10月5日}} - {{ill|Nokitsukesai|ja|檐付祭}}（のきつけさい） * {{ill|November 5|ja|11月5日}} - {{ill|Irakasai|ja|甍祭}}（いらかさい） ==== 2015 ==== * {{ill|February 26|ja|2月26日}} - {{ill|Mitosai|ja|御戸祭}}（みとさい）・{{ill|Mifunashiro Hōnō-shiki|ja|御船代奉納式}}（みふなしろほうのうしき）・{{ill|Araikiyome|ja|洗清}}（あらいきよめ） * {{ill|February 27|ja|2月27日}} - {{ill|Kotsukisai|ja|杵築祭}}（こつきさい）・{{ill|Gochinsai|ja|後鎮祭}}（ごちんさい）・{{ill|Kawahara Ōharai|ja|川原大祓}}（かわらおおはらい） * {{ill|February 28|ja|2月28日}} - {{ill|Okazari|ja|御飾}}（おかざり）・{{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御}}（せんぎょ） * {{ill|March 1|ja|3月1日}} - {{ill|Ōmike|ja|大御饌}}（おおみけ）・{{ill|Hōhei|ja|奉幣}} Above, the {{ill|Ritchūsai|ja|立柱祭}}, {{ill|Jōtōsai|ja|上棟祭}}, {{ill|Kotsukisai|ja|杵築祭}}, {{ill|Gochinsai|ja|後鎮祭}}, {{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御}}, and {{ill|Hōhei|ja|奉幣}} were scheduled according to the divine decision (*{{ill|Gojijō|ja|御治定}}*) of the reigning emperor。 Additionally, on {{ill|February 22|ja|2月22日}}, the *{{ill|Oshiraishi-mochi|ja|お白石持}}* ceremony took place, during which approximately 1,000 participants from the {{ill|Miyago Hōkendan|ja|宮後奉献団}} carried sacred stones (*{{ill|Oshiraishi|ja|御白石}}*) in a cart from the {{ill|Urakuchi Intersection|ja|浦口交差点}} to {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮}}, covering a distance of 1.2 km{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.chunichi.co.jp/article/mie/20150223/CK2015022302000028.html|title=次代につなぐ「エンヤ」 伊勢・月夜見宮でお白石持行事|author=中平雄大|publisher=[[中日新聞]]|date=2015-02-23|accessdate=2015-03-08|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150307161058/http://www.chunichi.co.jp/article/mie/20150223/CK2015022302000028.html|archivedate=2015-03-07}}。 This marked the completion of the *Oshiraishi-mochi* ceremonies for all auxiliary shrines (*{{ill|Betsugū|ja|別宮}}*)。 == 境内 == * 月夜見宮 - [[伊勢神宮]]{{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮}}（外宮）の別宮。社殿は外宮に準じ[[千木・鰹木|外削ぎの千木と、5本で奇数の鰹木]]を持つ萱葺の[[神明造]]で南面している。遷宮のための古殿地は東西に隣接している。外宮に準じ、20年に一度[[Jingū Shikinen Sengū|遷宮]]が行われる。その昔、月夜見宮の所在地の宮後町の民が役木を曳いて八日市場町にさしかかったときに宮後町で火事が起き、曳き手が消火のため帰ってしまったので、八日市場町の民が代わって役木を曳き、それ以来'''[[御木曳|御木曳初式]]'''（おきひきぞめしき）では八日市場町の民が月夜見宮に役木を奉曳することになったとの伝承がある。 * {{ill|Takagawara Shrine|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} - 祭神：月夜見尊御魂（つきよみのみことのみたま）。月夜見宮の境内にあるが伊勢神宮豊受大神宮（外宮）の[[摂社]]である。 * [[稲荷社]] * 宿衛屋 == 神路通り == [[File:Kamiji Street from Tsukiyomi no Miya.jpg|thumb|神路通り]] 外宮の北御門（きたみかど）から月夜見宮までの、幅員4m程度の1直線の道は「神が通る道」とされ、「'''神路通り'''（かみじどおり）」と呼ばれる。[[神路通り]]の項目を参照。 == 信者団体 == [[1960年]]（昭和35年）に伊勢市在住の崇敬者を中心に月夜見講が発足され、のちに月夜見宮奉賛会と改称した。月夜見宮奉賛会は毎年4月と9月の19日に神恩感謝の祭を行うなどの活動をしている。 == 交通 == * [[東海旅客鉄道|JR]][[参宮線]]・[[近畿日本鉄道|近鉄]][[近鉄山田線|山田線]][[伊勢市駅]]から徒歩約10分。 * 外宮北御門口から[[神路通り]]経由で徒歩約5分JTBパブリッシング（2011）：43ページ。 * [[三重交通]]新道バス停下車徒歩約3分、[[伊勢市コミュニティバス|伊勢市コミュニティバス「おかげバス」]]月夜見宮前バス停下車すぐ2013年7月20日から運行が開始された三重交通の「参宮バス」が「月夜見宮前」停留所に停車していたが、2015年3月31日をもって「月夜見宮前」停留所への乗り入れが廃止された。 * [[伊勢自動車道]][[伊勢インターチェンジ]]から約3km * 駐車場：鳥居前には2-4台しか駐車できないが、南面する道路に[[駐車場|パーキングメーター]]がある。 == 脚注 == {{Reflist}} == 参考文献 == * 『月夜見宮参拝のしおり』（発行：神宮司庁） * 『お伊勢さんを歩こう』（発行：伊勢神宮崇敬会） * 『お伊勢まいり』（発行：伊勢神宮崇敬会） * 『宇治山田市史』 * 金子延夫『玉城町史 二巻 －南伊勢の歴史と伝承－』三重県郷土資料叢書第91集、三重県郷土資料刊行会、昭和58年12月10日 * 出版事業本部 国内情報部 第三編集部 編『[[るるぶ]] お伊勢まいり』るるぶ情報版近畿21、通巻4615号、[[JTBパブリッシング]]、2014年5月1日、92p. ISBN 978-4-533-09761-4 * [[三橋健 (神道学者)|三橋健]]『伊勢神宮 日本人は何を祈ってきたのか』[[朝日新書]]416、[[朝日新聞出版]]、2013年8月30日、230p. ISBN 978-4-02-273516-4 * 矢野憲一『伊勢神宮―知られざる杜のうち』角川選書402、[[角川学芸出版]]、平成18年11月10日、270p. ISBN 4-04-703402-9 * 『伊勢神宮』楽学ブックス 神社1、JTBパブリッシング、2011年4月1日、143p. ISBN 978-4-533-08206-1 * 『日本人なら知っておきたい 伊勢神宮と125の社』タツミムック、[[辰巳出版]]、2013年11月1日、127p. ISBN 978-4-7778-1197-7 * 『いま行く!伊勢神宮お参りパーフェクトブック』みらい出版、2013年12月10日、107p. ISBN 978-4-907292-14-0 == See Also == * [[ツクヨミ]] * [[伊勢国の式内社一覧]] * {{ill|List of 125 Shrines of Ise|ja|神宮125社の一覧}} * [[神路通り]] == 外部リンク == {{commonscat|Tsukiyomi-no-miya (Geku)}} * [http://www.isejingu.or.jp/about/geku/tsukiyomi.html 月夜見宮] - 伊勢神宮公式サイト * [http://www.jingukaikan.jp/125mairi/m02/0202.html 月夜見宮（つきよみのみや） - 神宮会館] - 一般財団法人伊勢神宮崇敬会 * [http://www.ise-kanko.jp/base_data/base_data.php?info_cd=00269 伊勢市観光協会/月夜見宮] * [http://www.barifuri.com/tourcenter/data_kankou/tsukiyomi_1/index.html 月夜見宮（つきよみのみや）] - 伊勢志摩バリアフリーツアーセンター {{125 Shrines of Ise}} {{神道 横}} {{125 Shrines of Ise|つきよみのみや}} [[Category:125 Shrines of Ise]] [[Category:Completion tier 3]][[Category:tier 3]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)]] [[Category:Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)]][[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:Tsukiyominomiya]][[ja:月夜見宮]][[Category:Tsukiyominomiya]][[Category:伊勢国の式内社]] [[Category:伊勢市の神社]] [[Category:2015年竣工の日本の建築物]] [[Category:refreshing imported pages]][[Category:refreshing imported pages]] [[Category:category refresh]] [[Category:pgoodbye $1]][[Category:new pages]][[Category:Tsukiyominomiya]][[Category:pgoodbye $1]][[Category:new pages]] [[Category:fixing the kk issue]] [[Category:Tsukiyomi-no-Miya]] [[Category:U]][[Category: pages]] [[Category:Sqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqq]] [[Category:qqqq]] [[Category:q--q]] [[Category:qq]] [[Category:trimming off this bad category]][[sn:Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)]][[Category:trimming off this bad category]] [[en:Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)]] [[Category:New]]

{{distinguish|{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|2=es|3=Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|4=ja|5=月讀宮|lkt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya}}}} {{混同|月讀宮|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|2=es|3=Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|4=ja|5=月讀宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya}} {{神社 | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Geku Tsukiyomi no Miya in October 2016.jpg|270px]]
社殿 |名称 = 月夜見宮 |所在地 = [[三重県]][[伊勢市]]宮後一丁目3-19 |位置 = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|29|34.7|N|136|42|21.3|E|display=inline,title}} |祭神 = [[ツクヨミ|月夜見尊]]
月夜見尊荒御魂 |社格 = [[式内社]]（小）
{{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮}}別宮 |創建 = [[延長 (元号)|延長]]5年（[[927年]]）以前 |本殿 = [[神明造]] |例祭= |地図 = {{location map|Japan Mie|lat_deg=34|lat_min=29|lat_sec=34.7|lon_deg=136|lon_min=42|lon_sec=21.3|label=月夜見宮|position=top|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|34|29|34.7|N|136|42|21.3|E}}}} }} '''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya''' (月夜見宮) is a [[Shinto shrine|shrine]] located in Miyago, Ise City, Mie Prefecture辰巳出版（2013）：16ページ. It is a [[Betsugū]] of [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]] {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮}} (Outer Shrine)伊勢文化舎 編（2008）：39ページみらい出版（2013）：64ページ学研パブリッシング（2013）：69ページJTBパブリッシング（2011）：42ページ出版事業本部 国内情報部 第三編集部 編（2014）：34ページ三橋（2013）：124ページ。 It is a [[Shikinaisha]]. == Overview == [[File:Tsukiyomi-nomiya(Geku)_00.JPG|thumb|300px|right|Aerial view of Tsukiyomi-no-Miya]] Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is an auxiliary shrine (betsugu) of the Outer Shrine (Geku), located about 300 meters north of Geku and approximately 500 meters west of {{ill|Ise City Station|ja|伊勢市駅}}. It enshrines two deities within the same shrine building: {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto|ja|月夜見尊}} (Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto) and his fierce spirit, **Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto-no-Aramitama** (荒御魂 of Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto) . Unlike the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya}} auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine (Naiku), where Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto and his Aramitama are enshrined separately, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya uniquely houses both deities within a single structure . The only other auxiliary shrines that enshrine two deities in one building are {{ill|Kaze-no-Miya|ja|風宮}} (Kaze-no-Miya) of the Outer Shrine and {{ill|Kazahinomi-no-Miya|ja|風日祈宮|lt=Kazahi-no-Miya}} of the Inner Shrine, both enshrining Shinatsuhiko-no-Mikoto (級長津彦命) and Shinatsuhime-no-Mikoto (級長戸辺命). Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is the only auxiliary shrine of the Outer Shrine located outside the main precincts . Despite being in the urban area of Ise City, its grounds maintain a serene atmosphere . The moat surrounding three sides of the precinct is thought to be a remnant of a tributary of the {{ill|Miyagawa River (Mie Prefecture)|ja|宮川 (三重県)}} . The {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 37|ja|三重県道37号鳥羽松阪線}} runs along the northern side of the moat and serves as the route for the **Hatsuhobiki** (初穂曳), a festival procession held every October in conjunction with the {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}. During this event, decorated carts carry the first harvested rice offerings to the Outer Shrine. Adjacent to the right rear of the shrine building is the auxiliary shrine of {{ill|Takagawara Shrine|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} . To the left rear stands an {{ill|Inari shrine|ja|稲荷}} , and to the right is a large sacred camphor tree (大楠), where many people offer prayers . Like other auxiliary shrines outside the main precincts, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya has a **Shukueiya** (宿衛屋), a guardhouse where Shinto priests are present during visiting hours to distribute amulets, offer kagura performances, and manage food offerings (御饌). == Worshipped Deities (Saijin) == {{see also|{{ill|Saijin|ja|祭神}}}} * {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|ja|ツクヨミ}}（つきよみのみこと） * {{nihongo|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto-no-Ara-Mitama|月夜見尊荒御魂}} : {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|ja|月夜見尊}} is the same deity as {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|ja|月讀尊}}, the enshrined deity of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月讀宮}}, an auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine (Naikū) of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮}}. He is the brother of {{ill|Amaterasu Ōmikami|ja|天照大神}}. Since agricultural activities historically relied on the lunar calendar ({{ill|Lunisolar calendar|ja|太陰暦}}), he has been worshipped as a deity of agriculture. Additionally, he is also considered a river deity of {{ill|Takagawara|ja|高河原}} and a deity associated with women. According to the *{{ill|Jinmyō Hisho|ja|神名秘書}}*, his {{ill|Shintai|ja|神体}} (sacred object) is a {{ill|mirror|ja|鏡}}. == Festivals == The shrine follows a festival schedule similar to that of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮}}, with offerings from the {{ill|Imperial House of Japan|ja|皇室}} during prayers for the harvest (*{{ill|Kinensai|ja|祈年祭}}*), seasonal festivals (*{{ill|Tsukinamisai|ja|月次祭}}*), and major thanksgiving ceremonies (*{{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}* and *{{ill|Niinamesai|ja|新嘗祭}}*). * **January** * *{{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭}}* (New Year's Festival) – {{ill|January 1|ja|1月1日}} * A festival celebrating the new year and praying for the eternal prosperity of the imperial lineage. * *{{ill|Genshi-sai|ja|元始祭}}* (Imperial Foundation Festival) – {{ill|January 3|ja|1月3日}} * A festival celebrating the origins of the imperial rule. * **February** * *{{ill|Kenkoku Kinen-sai|ja|建国記念祭}}* (National Foundation Festival) – {{ill|February 11|ja|2月11日}} * Celebrating the founding of Japan by {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|ja|神武天皇}}. * *{{ill|Kinensai|ja|祈年祭}}* (Prayer Festival) – {{ill|February 18|ja|2月18日}} * A ceremony held early in the year to pray for abundant grain harvests and national peace. * *{{ill|Tenchō-sai|ja|天長祭}}* (Emperor’s Birthday Festival) – {{ill|February 23|ja|2月23日}} * A festival honoring the birthday of {{ill|Emperor Naruhito|ja|徳仁天皇}}. * **May** * *{{ill|Kazahinomi-sai|ja|風日祈祭}}* (Wind and Sun Festival) – {{ill|May 14|ja|5月14日}} * Offerings are made at the Outer Shrine, Inner Shrine, and affiliated shrines to pray for protection from storms and a bountiful harvest. * **June** * *{{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭}}* (Monthly Festival) – {{ill|June 18|ja|6月18日}}–{{ill|June 19|ja|6月19日}} * A biannual festival held in June and December to pray for the well-being of the nation and the emperor. Together with *{{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}*, these are called the *Three Great Festivals* (三節祭 or 三時祭). * **August** * *{{ill|Kazahinomi-sai|ja|風日祈祭}}* (Wind and Sun Festival) – {{ill|August 4|ja|8月4日}} * A repetition of the May festival to pray for good weather and agricultural prosperity. * **October** * *{{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}* (First Fruits Festival) – {{ill|October 18|ja|10月18日}}–{{ill|October 19|ja|10月19日}} * A festival where priests present freshly harvested grains as offerings to the gods. * **November** * *{{ill|Niinamesai|ja|新嘗祭}}* (New Harvest Festival) – {{ill|November 24|ja|11月24日}} * A festival in which the emperor offers the season’s first grains to the gods and partakes in them as an act of gratitude. * **December** * *{{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭}}* (Monthly Festival) – {{ill|December 18|ja|12月18日}}–{{ill|December 19|ja|12月19日}} === {{ill|Shikinen Sengu|ja|式年遷宮}} === [[File:Sengu of Tsukiyomi no Miya, August 2014.jpg|thumb|{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮}} ahead of {{ill|Ritchūsai|ja|立柱祭}} (photo taken on August 11, 2014) The shrine at the time is on the left, and the shrine under construction is on the right.]]The festivals and dates of the 62nd annual {{ill|Shikinen Sengu|ja|式年遷宮}} of the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮}} are as follows{{Cite web|和書|url=http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2259/|title=伊勢神宮外宮別宮のもう一つの「月の神様」もお引っ越し―残すは風宮|publisher=[[伊勢志摩経済新聞]]|date=2015-03-03|accessdate=2015-03-07|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150307142246/http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2259/|archivedate=2015-03-07}}{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.isejingu.or.jp/sikinen_2.html|title=月讀宮以下12別宮の遷宮 - 伊勢神宮|publisher=神宮司庁|accessdate=2015-03-07|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150210061619/http://www.isejingu.or.jp/sikinen_2.html|archivedate=2015-02-10}}。 ==== 2014 ==== * {{ill|August 20|ja|8月20日}} - {{ill|Ritchūsai|ja|立柱祭}}（りっちゅうさい）・{{ill|Jōtōsai|ja|上棟祭}}（じょうとうさい） * {{ill|October 5|ja|10月5日}} - {{ill|Nokitsukesai|ja|檐付祭}}（のきつけさい） * {{ill|November 5|ja|11月5日}} - {{ill|Irakasai|ja|甍祭}}（いらかさい） ==== 2015 ==== * {{ill|February 26|ja|2月26日}} - {{ill|Mitosai|ja|御戸祭}}（みとさい）・{{ill|Mifunashiro Hōnō-shiki|ja|御船代奉納式}}（みふなしろほうのうしき）・{{ill|Araikiyome|ja|洗清}}（あらいきよめ） * {{ill|February 27|ja|2月27日}} - {{ill|Kotsukisai|ja|杵築祭}}（こつきさい）・{{ill|Gochinsai|ja|後鎮祭}}（ごちんさい）・{{ill|Kawahara Ōharai|ja|川原大祓}}（かわらおおはらい） * {{ill|February 28|ja|2月28日}} - {{ill|Okazari|ja|御飾}}（おかざり）・{{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御}}（せんぎょ） * {{ill|March 1|ja|3月1日}} - {{ill|Ōmike|ja|大御饌}}（おおみけ）・{{ill|Hōhei|ja|奉幣}} Above, the {{ill|Ritchūsai|ja|立柱祭}}, {{ill|Jōtōsai|ja|上棟祭}}, {{ill|Kotsukisai|ja|杵築祭}}, {{ill|Gochinsai|ja|後鎮祭}}, {{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御}}, and {{ill|Hōhei|ja|奉幣}} were scheduled according to the divine decision (*{{ill|Gojijō|ja|御治定}}*) of the reigning emperor。 Additionally, on {{ill|February 22|ja|2月22日}}, the *{{ill|Oshiraishi-mochi|ja|お白石持}}* ceremony took place, during which approximately 1,000 participants from the {{ill|Miyago Hōkendan|ja|宮後奉献団}} carried sacred stones (*{{ill|Oshiraishi|ja|御白石}}*) in a cart from the {{ill|Urakuchi Intersection|ja|浦口交差点}} to {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮}}, covering a distance of 1.2 km{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.chunichi.co.jp/article/mie/20150223/CK2015022302000028.html|title=次代につなぐ「エンヤ」 伊勢・月夜見宮でお白石持行事|author=中平雄大|publisher=[[中日新聞]]|date=2015-02-23|accessdate=2015-03-08|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150307161058/http://www.chunichi.co.jp/article/mie/20150223/CK2015022302000028.html|archivedate=2015-03-07}}。 This marked the completion of the *Oshiraishi-mochi* ceremonies for all auxiliary shrines (*{{ill|Betsugū|ja|別宮}}*)。 == 境内 == * 月夜見宮 - [[伊勢神宮]]{{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮}}（外宮）の別宮。社殿は外宮に準じ[[千木・鰹木|外削ぎの千木と、5本で奇数の鰹木]]を持つ萱葺の[[神明造]]で南面している。遷宮のための古殿地は東西に隣接している。外宮に準じ、20年に一度[[Jingū Shikinen Sengū|遷宮]]が行われる。その昔、月夜見宮の所在地の宮後町の民が役木を曳いて八日市場町にさしかかったときに宮後町で火事が起き、曳き手が消火のため帰ってしまったので、八日市場町の民が代わって役木を曳き、それ以来'''[[御木曳|御木曳初式]]'''（おきひきぞめしき）では八日市場町の民が月夜見宮に役木を奉曳することになったとの伝承がある。 * {{ill|Takagawara Shrine|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} - 祭神：月夜見尊御魂（つきよみのみことのみたま）。月夜見宮の境内にあるが伊勢神宮豊受大神宮（外宮）の[[摂社]]である。 * [[稲荷社]] * 宿衛屋 == 神路通り == [[File:Kamiji Street from Tsukiyomi no Miya.jpg|thumb|神路通り]] 外宮の北御門（きたみかど）から月夜見宮までの、幅員4m程度の1直線の道は「神が通る道」とされ、「'''神路通り'''（かみじどおり）」と呼ばれる。[[神路通り]]の項目を参照。 == 信者団体 == [[1960年]]（昭和35年）に伊勢市在住の崇敬者を中心に月夜見講が発足され、のちに月夜見宮奉賛会と改称した。月夜見宮奉賛会は毎年4月と9月の19日に神恩感謝の祭を行うなどの活動をしている。 == 交通 == * [[東海旅客鉄道|JR]][[参宮線]]・[[近畿日本鉄道|近鉄]][[近鉄山田線|山田線]][[伊勢市駅]]から徒歩約10分。 * 外宮北御門口から[[神路通り]]経由で徒歩約5分JTBパブリッシング（2011）：43ページ。 * [[三重交通]]新道バス停下車徒歩約3分、[[伊勢市コミュニティバス|伊勢市コミュニティバス「おかげバス」]]月夜見宮前バス停下車すぐ2013年7月20日から運行が開始された三重交通の「参宮バス」が「月夜見宮前」停留所に停車していたが、2015年3月31日をもって「月夜見宮前」停留所への乗り入れが廃止された。 * [[伊勢自動車道]][[伊勢インターチェンジ]]から約3km * 駐車場：鳥居前には2-4台しか駐車できないが、南面する道路に[[駐車場|パーキングメーター]]がある。 == 脚注 == {{Reflist}} == 参考文献 == * 『月夜見宮参拝のしおり』（発行：神宮司庁） * 『お伊勢さんを歩こう』（発行：伊勢神宮崇敬会） * 『お伊勢まいり』（発行：伊勢神宮崇敬会） * 『宇治山田市史』 * 金子延夫『玉城町史 二巻 －南伊勢の歴史と伝承－』三重県郷土資料叢書第91集、三重県郷土資料刊行会、昭和58年12月10日 * 出版事業本部 国内情報部 第三編集部 編『[[るるぶ]] お伊勢まいり』るるぶ情報版近畿21、通巻4615号、[[JTBパブリッシング]]、2014年5月1日、92p. 社殿 |名称 = 月夜見宮 |所在地 = [[三重県]][[伊勢市]]宮後一丁目3-19 |位置 = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|29|34.7|N|136|42|21.3|E|display=inline,title}} |祭神 = [[ツクヨミ|月夜見尊]]
月夜見尊荒御魂 |社格 = [[式内社]]（小）
{{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮}}別宮 |創建 = [[延長 (元号)|延長]]5年（[[927年]]）以前 |本殿 = [[神明造]] |例祭= |地図 = {{location map|Japan Mie|lat_deg=34|lat_min=29|lat_sec=34.7|lon_deg=136|lon_min=42|lon_sec=21.3|label=月夜見宮|position=top|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|34|29|34.7|N|136|42|21.3|E}}}} }} '''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya''' (月夜見宮) is a [[Shinto shrine|shrine]] located in Miyago, Ise City, Mie Prefecture辰巳出版（2013）：16ページ. It is a [[Betsugū]] of [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]] {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮}} (Outer Shrine)伊勢文化舎 編（2008）：39ページみらい出版（2013）：64ページ学研パブリッシング（2013）：69ページJTBパブリッシング（2011）：42ページ出版事業本部 国内情報部 第三編集部 編（2014）：34ページ三橋（2013）：124ページ。 It is a [[Shikinaisha]]. == Overview == [[File:Tsukiyomi-nomiya(Geku)_00.JPG|thumb|300px|right|Aerial view of Tsukiyomi-no-Miya]] Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is an auxiliary shrine (betsugu) of the Outer Shrine (Geku), located about 300 meters north of Geku and approximately 500 meters west of {{ill|Ise City Station|ja|伊勢市駅}}. It enshrines two deities within the same shrine building: {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto|ja|月夜見尊}} (Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto) and his fierce spirit, **Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto-no-Aramitama** (荒御魂 of Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto) . Unlike the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya}} auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine (Naiku), where Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto and his Aramitama are enshrined separately, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya uniquely houses both deities within a single structure . The only other auxiliary shrines that enshrine two deities in one building are {{ill|Kaze-no-Miya|ja|風宮}} (Kaze-no-Miya) of the Outer Shrine and {{ill|Kazahinomi-no-Miya|ja|風日祈宮|lt=Kazahi-no-Miya}} of the Inner Shrine, both enshrining Shinatsuhiko-no-Mikoto (級長津彦命) and Shinatsuhime-no-Mikoto (級長戸辺命). Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is the only auxiliary shrine of the Outer Shrine located outside the main precincts . Despite being in the urban area of Ise City, its grounds maintain a serene atmosphere . The moat surrounding three sides of the precinct is thought to be a remnant of a tributary of the {{ill|Miyagawa River (Mie Prefecture)|ja|宮川 (三重県)}} . The {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 37|ja|三重県道37号鳥羽松阪線}} runs along the northern side of the moat and serves as the route for the **Hatsuhobiki** (初穂曳), a festival procession held every October in conjunction with the {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}. During this event, decorated carts carry the first harvested rice offerings to the Outer Shrine. Adjacent to the right rear of the shrine building is the auxiliary shrine of {{ill|Takagawara Shrine|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}} . To the left rear stands an {{ill|Inari shrine|ja|稲荷}} , and to the right is a large sacred camphor tree (大楠), where many people offer prayers . Like other auxiliary shrines outside the main precincts, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya has a **Shukueiya** (宿衛屋), a guardhouse where Shinto priests are present during visiting hours to distribute amulets, offer kagura performances, and manage food offerings (御饌). == Worshipped Deities (Saijin) == {{see also|{{ill|Saijin|ja|祭神}}}} * {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|ja|ツクヨミ}}（つきよみのみこと） * {{nihongo|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto-no-Ara-Mitama|月夜見尊荒御魂}} : {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|ja|月夜見尊}} is the same deity as {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|ja|月讀尊}}, the enshrined deity of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月讀宮}}, an auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine (Naikū) of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮}}. He is the brother of {{ill|Amaterasu Ōmikami|ja|天照大神}}. Since agricultural activities historically relied on the lunar calendar ({{ill|Lunisolar calendar|ja|太陰暦}}), he has been worshipped as a deity of agriculture. Additionally, he is also considered a river deity of {{ill|Takagawara|ja|高河原}} and a deity associated with women. According to the *{{ill|Jinmyō Hisho|ja|神名秘書}}*, his {{ill|Shintai|ja|神体}} (sacred object) is a {{ill|mirror|ja|鏡}}. == Festivals == The shrine follows a festival schedule similar to that of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮}}, with offerings from the {{ill|Imperial House of Japan|ja|皇室}} during prayers for the harvest (*{{ill|Kinensai|ja|祈年祭}}*), seasonal festivals (*{{ill|Tsukinamisai|ja|月次祭}}*), and major thanksgiving ceremonies (*{{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}* and *{{ill|Niinamesai|ja|新嘗祭}}*). * **January** * *{{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭}}* (New Year's Festival) – {{ill|January 1|ja|1月1日}} * A festival celebrating the new year and praying for the eternal prosperity of the imperial lineage. * *{{ill|Genshi-sai|ja|元始祭}}* (Imperial Foundation Festival) – {{ill|January 3|ja|1月3日}} * A festival celebrating the origins of the imperial rule. * **February** * *{{ill|Kenkoku Kinen-sai|ja|建国記念祭}}* (National Foundation Festival) – {{ill|February 11|ja|2月11日}} * Celebrating the founding of Japan by {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|ja|神武天皇}}. * *{{ill|Kinensai|ja|祈年祭}}* (Prayer Festival) – {{ill|February 18|ja|2月18日}} * A ceremony held early in the year to pray for abundant grain harvests and national peace. * *{{ill|Tenchō-sai|ja|天長祭}}* (Emperor’s Birthday Festival) – {{ill|February 23|ja|2月23日}} * A festival honoring the birthday of {{ill|Emperor Naruhito|ja|徳仁天皇}}. * **May** * *{{ill|Kazahinomi-sai|ja|風日祈祭}}* (Wind and Sun Festival) – {{ill|May 14|ja|5月14日}} * Offerings are made at the Outer Shrine, Inner Shrine, and affiliated shrines to pray for protection from storms and a bountiful harvest. * **June** * *{{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭}}* (Monthly Festival) – {{ill|June 18|ja|6月18日}}–{{ill|June 19|ja|6月19日}} * A biannual festival held in June and December to pray for the well-being of the nation and the emperor. Together with *{{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}*, these are called the *Three Great Festivals* (三節祭 or 三時祭). * **August** * *{{ill|Kazahinomi-sai|ja|風日祈祭}}* (Wind and Sun Festival) – {{ill|August 4|ja|8月4日}} * A repetition of the May festival to pray for good weather and agricultural prosperity. * **October** * *{{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}* (First Fruits Festival) – {{ill|October 18|ja|10月18日}}–{{ill|October 19|ja|10月19日}} * A festival where priests present freshly harvested grains as offerings to the gods. * **November** * *{{ill|Niinamesai|ja|新嘗祭}}* (New Harvest Festival) – {{ill|November 24|ja|11月24日}} * A festival in which the emperor offers the season’s first grains to the gods and partakes in them as an act of gratitude. * **December** * *{{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭}}* (Monthly Festival) – {{ill|December 18|ja|12月18日}}–{{ill|December 19|ja|12月19日}} === {{ill|Shikinen Sengu|ja|式年遷宮}} === [[File:Sengu of Tsukiyomi no Miya, August 2014.jpg|thumb|{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮}} ahead of {{ill|Ritchūsai|ja|立柱祭}} (photo taken on August 11, 2014) The shrine at the time is on the left, and the shrine under construction is on the right.]]The festivals and dates of the 62nd annual {{ill|Shikinen Sengu|ja|式年遷宮}} of the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮}} are as follows{{Cite web|和書|url=http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2259/|title=伊勢神宮外宮別宮のもう一つの「月の神様」もお引っ越し―残すは風宮|publisher=[[伊勢志摩経済新聞]]|date=2015-03-03|accessdate=2015-03-07|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150307142246/http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2259/|archivedate=2015-03-07}}{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.isejingu.or.jp/sikinen_2.html|title=月讀宮以下12別宮の遷宮 - 伊勢神宮|publisher=神宮司庁|accessdate=2015-03-07|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150210061619/http://www.isejingu.or.jp/sikinen_2.html|archivedate=2015-02-10}}。 ==== 2014 ==== * {{ill|August 20|ja|8月20日}} - {{ill|Okazari|ja|御飾}}（おかざり）・{{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御}}（せんぎょ） * {{ill|March 1|ja|3月1日}} - {{ill|Ōmike|ja|大御饌}}（おおみけ）・{{ill|Hōhei|ja|奉幣}} Above, the {{ill|Ritchūsai|ja|立柱祭}}, {{ill|Jōtōsai|ja|上棟祭}}, {{ill|Kotsukisai|ja|杵築祭}}, {{ill|Gochinsai|ja|後鎮祭}}, {{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御}}, and {{ill|Hōhei|ja|奉幣}} were scheduled according to the divine decision (*{{ill|Gojijō|ja|御治定}}*) of the reigning emperor。 Additionally, on {{ill|February 22|ja|2月22日}}, the *{{ill|Oshiraishi-mochi|ja|お白石持}}* ceremony took place, during which approximately 1,000 participants from the {{ill|Miyago Hōkendan|ja|宮後奉献団}} carried sacred stones (*{{ill|Oshiraishi|ja|御白石}}*) in a cart from the {{ill|Urakuchi Intersection|ja|浦口交差点}} to {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮}}, covering a distance of 1.2 km{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.chunichi.co.jp/article/mie/20150223/CK2015022302000028.html|title=次代につなぐ「エンヤ」 伊勢・月夜見宮でお白石持行事|author=中平雄大|publisher=[[中日新聞]]|date=2015-02-23|accessdate=2015-03-08|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150307161058/http://www.chunichi.co.jp/article/mie/20150223/CK2015022302000028.html|archivedate=2015-03-07}}。 This marked the completion of the *Oshiraishi-mochi* ceremonies for all auxiliary shrines (*{{ill|Betsugū|ja|別宮}}*)。 == Shrine Grounds (境内) == * **Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (月夜見宮)** - A **Betsugū** (auxiliary shrine) of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮}} (Outer Shrine of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮}}). The shrine’s **architecture follows Shinmei-zukuri** and features **chigi (forked finials) cut horizontally** and **five katsuogi (short decorative logs)**, **a thatched roof**, and **a south-facing orientation**. - **Shikinen Sengu (式年遷宮)**: The shrine is **reconstructed every 20 years** according to the ancient practice of **Shikinen Sengu**. The **former shrine grounds** (古殿地, kodenchi) are located directly to the east and west of the current shrine. - **Traditional Legend**: It is said that in the past, when the people of **Miyago Town** were carrying **sacred timber (役木, yakugi)** for shrine reconstruction, they **passed through Yokaichiba Town**. At that moment, **a fire broke out in Miyago Town**, and the timber carriers **rushed back to extinguish it**. As a result, the people of Yokaichiba took over the role of **carrying the sacred timber**. Since then, in the **Okihikizome-shiki (御木曳初式, First Timber-Carrying Ceremony)**, **the people of Yokaichiba** have traditionally taken on the **honor of bringing the sacred timber to Tsukiyomi-no-Miya**. * **{{ill|Takagawara Shrine|ja|皇大神宮|1=Kōtai Jingū|2=ja|3=皇大神宮|4=zh|5=皇大神宮}}** - Dedicated to **Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto no Mitama (月夜見尊御魂, Spirit of Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto)**. Though located within **Tsukiyomi-no-Miya**, it is actually **a Sessha (摂社, auxiliary shrine) of Toyouke Daijingu (Outer Shrine).** * **{{ill|Inari Shrine|ja|稲荷社}}** – A shrine dedicated to **Inari**, the deity of **prosperity and agriculture**. * **Shukueya (宿衛屋)** – A **guardhouse** for shrine officials. --- == Kamiji Street (神路通り) == [[File:Kamiji Street from Tsukiyomi no Miya.jpg|thumb|Kamiji Street]] A **narrow, 4-meter-wide straight path** connects the **North Gate (北御門, Kita-mikado) of the Outer Shrine** to **Tsukiyomi-no-Miya**. This road is known as **"Kamiji Street" (神路通り, Kamiji-dōri), meaning "Path of the Gods,"** as it is **believed to be the route taken by deities.** See {{ill|Kamiji Street|ja|神路通り}} for details. --- == Worshipers' Association (信者団体) == In **1960 (Shōwa 35)**, a group of **Ise City residents** founded the **Tsukiyomi-kō (月夜見講)**, which was later renamed the **Tsukiyomi-no-Miya Hōsankai (月夜見宮奉賛会, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya Worshipers' Association).** - This organization **holds annual thanksgiving festivals** on **April 19 and September 19**, among other activities. --- == Access (交通) == * **Train:** - **10-minute walk** from **{{ill|Ise City Station|ja|伊勢市駅}}** (served by **JR {{ill|Sangu Line|ja|参宮線}}** & **Kintetsu {{ill|Yamada Line|ja|近鉄山田線}}**). - **5-minute walk** from the **North Gate of the Outer Shrine** via **Kamiji Street**. * **Bus:** - **3-minute walk** from **Shindō Bus Stop** (**{{ill|Mie Kotsu|ja|三重交通}} Bus**). - **Tsukiyomi-no-Miya-mae Bus Stop** (served by the **{{ill|Ise City Community Bus|ja|伊勢市コミュニティバス}}**). - Note: From **July 20, 2013**, the **Sangu Bus** operated by Mie Kotsu stopped at **Tsukiyomi-no-Miya-mae**, but this service was **discontinued on March 31, 2015**. * **Car:** - **Approx. 3 km** from **{{ill|Ise Interchange|ja|伊勢インターチェンジ}} (Ise Expressway).** - **Parking:** There are **only 2-4 parking spaces in front of the torii gate**, but **metered parking** is available on the south side of the street. --- [[Category:Shinto shrines in Japan]] [[Category:Ise Grand Shrine]] [[Category:Translated pages]] [[ja:月夜見宮]] == 脚注 == {{Reflist}} == 参考文献 == * 『月夜見宮参拝のしおり』（発行：神宮司庁） * 『お伊勢さんを歩こう』（発行：伊勢神宮崇敬会） * 『お伊勢まいり』（発行：伊勢神宮崇敬会） * 『宇治山田市史』 * 金子延夫『玉城町史 二巻 －南伊勢の歴史と伝承－』三重県郷土資料叢書第91集、三重県郷土資料刊行会、昭和58年12月10日 * 出版事業本部 国内情報部 第三編集部 編『[[るるぶ]] お伊勢まいり』るるぶ情報版近畿21、通巻4615号、[[JTBパブリッシング]]、2014年5月1日、92p. ISBN 978-4-533-09761-4 * [[三橋健 (神道学者)|三橋健]]『伊勢神宮 日本人は何を祈ってきたのか』[[朝日新書]]416、[[朝日新聞出版]]、2013年8月30日、230p. ISBN 978-4-02-273516-4 * 矢野憲一『伊勢神宮―知られざる杜のうち』角川選書402、[[角川学芸出版]]、平成18年11月10日、270p. ISBN 4-04-703402-9 * 『伊勢神宮』楽学ブックス 神社1、JTBパブリッシング、2011年4月1日、143p. ISBN 978-4-533-08206-1 * 『日本人なら知っておきたい 伊勢神宮と125の社』タツミムック、[[辰巳出版]]、2013年11月1日、127p. ISBN 978-4-907292-14-0 == See Also == * [[ツクヨミ]] * [[伊勢国の式内社一覧]] * {{ill|List of 125 Shrines of Ise|ja|神宮125社の一覧}} * [[神路通り]] == 外部リンク == {{commonscat|Tsukiyomi-no-miya (Geku)}} * [http://www.isejingu.or.jp/about/geku/tsukiyomi.html 月夜見宮] - 伊勢神宮公式サイト * [http://www.jingukaikan.jp/125mairi/m02/0202.html 月夜見宮（つきよみのみや） - 神宮会館] - 一般財団法人伊勢神宮崇敬会 * [http://www.ise-kanko.jp/base_data/base_data.php?info_cd=00269 伊勢市観光協会/月夜見宮] * [http://www.barifuri.com/tourcenter/data_kankou/tsukiyomi_1/index.html 月夜見宮（つきよみのみや）] - 伊勢志摩バリアフリーツアーセンター {{125 Shrines of Ise}} {{神道 横}} {{125 Shrines of Ise|つきよみのみや}} [[Category:125 Shrines of Ise]] [[Category:Completion tier 3]][[Category:tier 3]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)]] [[Category:Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)]][[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:Tsukiyominomiya]][[ja:月夜見宮]][[Category:Tsukiyominomiya]][[Category:伊勢国の式内社]] [[Category:伊勢市の神社]] [[Category:2015年竣工の日本の建築物]] [[Category:refreshing imported pages]][[Category:refreshing imported pages]] [[Category:category refresh]] [[Category:pgoodbye $1]][[Category:new pages]][[Category:Tsukiyominomiya]][[Category:pgoodbye $1]][[Category:new pages]] [[Category:fixing the kk issue]] [[Category:Tsukiyomi-no-Miya]] [[Category:U]][[Category: pages]] [[Category:Sqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqq]] [[Category:qqqq]] [[Category:q--q]] [[Category:qq]] [[Category:trimming off this bad category]][[sn:Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)]][[Category:trimming off this bad category]] [[en:Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)]] [[Category:New]]

{{distinguish|{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|2=es|3=Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|4=ja|5=月讀宮|lkt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya}}}} {{混同|月讀宮|1=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|2=es|3=Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|4=ja|5=月讀宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya}} {{神社 | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = [[File:Geku Tsukiyomi no Miya in October 2016.jpg|270px]]
社殿 |名称 = 月夜見宮 |所在地 = [[三重県]][[伊勢市]]宮後一丁目3-19 |位置 = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|34|29|34.7|N|136|42|21.3|E|display=inline,title}} |祭神 = [[ツクヨミ|月夜見尊]]
月夜見尊荒御魂 |社格 = [[式内社]]（小）
{{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮}}別宮 |創建 = [[延長 (元号)|延長]]5年（[[927年]]）以前 |本殿 = [[神明造]] |例祭= |地図 = {{location map|Japan Mie|lat_deg=34|lat_min=29|lat_sec=34.7|lon_deg=136|lon_min=42|lon_sec=21.3|label=月夜見宮|position=top|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|34|29|34.7|N|136|42|21.3|E}}}} }} '''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya''' (月夜見宮) is a [[Shinto shrine|shrine]] located in Miyago, Ise City, Mie Prefecture辰巳出版（2013）：16ページ. It is a [[Betsugū]] of [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]] {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮}} (Outer Shrine)伊勢文化舎 編（2008）：39ページみらい出版（2013）：64ページ学研パブリッシング（2013）：69ページJTBパブリッシング（2011）：42ページ出版事業本部 国内情報部 第三編集部 編（2014）：34ページ三橋（2013）：124ページ。 It is a [[Shikinaisha]]. == Overview == [[File:Tsukiyomi-nomiya(Geku)_00.JPG|thumb|300px|right|Aerial view of Tsukiyomi-no-Miya]] Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is an auxiliary shrine (betsugu) of the Outer Shrine (Geku), located about 300 meters north of Geku and approximately 500 meters west of {{ill|Ise City Station|ja|伊勢市駅}}. It enshrines two deities within the same shrine building: {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto|ja|月夜見尊}} (Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto) and his fierce spirit, **Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto-no-Aramitama** (荒御魂 of Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto) . Unlike the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya}} auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine (Naiku), where Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto and his Aramitama are enshrined separately, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya uniquely houses both deities within a single structure . The only other auxiliary shrines that enshrine two deities in one building are {{ill|Kaze-no-Miya|ja|風宮}} (Kaze-no-Miya) of the Outer Shrine and {{ill|Kazahinomi-no-Miya|ja|風日祈宮|lt=Kazahi-no-Miya}} of the Inner Shrine, both enshrining Shinatsuhiko-no-Mikoto (級長津彦命) and Shinatsuhime-no-Mikoto (級長戸辺命). Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is the only auxiliary shrine of the Outer Shrine located outside the main precincts . Despite being in the urban area of Ise City, its grounds maintain a serene atmosphere . The moat surrounding three sides of the precinct is thought to be a remnant of a tributary of the {{ill|Miyagawa River (Mie Prefecture)|ja|宮川 (三重県)}} . The {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 37|ja|三重県道37号鳥羽松阪線}} runs along the northern side of the moat and serves as the route for the **Hatsuhobiki** (初穂曳), a festival procession held every October in conjunction with the {{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}. During this event, decorated carts carry the first harvested rice offerings to the Outer Shrine. Adjacent to the right rear of the shrine building is the auxiliary shrine of {{ill|Takagawara Shrine|ja|高河原神社|comment=no clue what happened there}} . To the left rear stands an {{ill|Inari shrine|ja|稲荷}} , and to the right is a large sacred camphor tree (大楠), where many people offer prayers . Like other auxiliary shrines outside the main precincts, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya has a **Shukueiya** (宿衛屋), a guardhouse where Shinto priests are present during visiting hours to distribute amulets, offer kagura performances, and manage food offerings (御饌). == Worshipped Deities (Saijin) == {{see also|{{ill|Saijin|ja|祭神}}}} * {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|ja|ツクヨミ}}（つきよみのみこと） * {{nihongo|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto-no-Ara-Mitama|月夜見尊荒御魂}} : {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|ja|月夜見尊}} is the same deity as {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|ja|月讀尊}}, the enshrined deity of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月讀宮}}, an auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine (Naikū) of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮}}. He is the brother of {{ill|Amaterasu Ōmikami|ja|天照大神}}. Since agricultural activities historically relied on the lunar calendar ({{ill|Lunisolar calendar|ja|太陰暦}}), he has been worshipped as a deity of agriculture. Additionally, he is also considered a river deity of {{ill|Takagawara|ja|高河原}} and a deity associated with women. According to the *{{ill|Jinmyō Hisho|ja|神名秘書}}*, his {{ill|Shintai|ja|神体}} (sacred object) is a {{ill|mirror|ja|鏡}}. == Festivals == The shrine follows a festival schedule similar to that of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮}}, with offerings from the {{ill|Imperial House of Japan|ja|皇室}} during prayers for the harvest (*{{ill|Kinensai|ja|祈年祭}}*), seasonal festivals (*{{ill|Tsukinamisai|ja|月次祭}}*), and major thanksgiving ceremonies (*{{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}* and *{{ill|Niinamesai|ja|新嘗祭}}*). * **January** * *{{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭}}* (New Year's Festival) – {{ill|January 1|ja|1月1日}} * A festival celebrating the new year and praying for the eternal prosperity of the imperial lineage. * *{{ill|Genshi-sai|ja|元始祭}}* (Imperial Foundation Festival) – {{ill|January 3|ja|1月3日}} * A festival celebrating the origins of the imperial rule. * **February** * *{{ill|Kenkoku Kinen-sai|ja|建国記念祭}}* (National Foundation Festival) – {{ill|February 11|ja|2月11日}} * Celebrating the founding of Japan by {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|ja|神武天皇}}. * *{{ill|Kinensai|ja|祈年祭}}* (Prayer Festival) – {{ill|February 18|ja|2月18日}} * A ceremony held early in the year to pray for abundant grain harvests and national peace. * *{{ill|Tenchō-sai|ja|天長祭}}* (Emperor’s Birthday Festival) – {{ill|February 23|ja|2月23日}} * A festival honoring the birthday of {{ill|Emperor Naruhito|ja|徳仁天皇}}. * **May** * *{{ill|Kazahinomi-sai|ja|風日祈祭}}* (Wind and Sun Festival) – {{ill|May 14|ja|5月14日}} * Offerings are made at the Outer Shrine, Inner Shrine, and affiliated shrines to pray for protection from storms and a bountiful harvest. * **June** * *{{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭}}* (Monthly Festival) – {{ill|June 18|ja|6月18日}}–{{ill|June 19|ja|6月19日}} * A biannual festival held in June and December to pray for the well-being of the nation and the emperor. Together with *{{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}*, these are called the *Three Great Festivals* (三節祭 or 三時祭). * **August** * *{{ill|Kazahinomi-sai|ja|風日祈祭}}* (Wind and Sun Festival) – {{ill|August 4|ja|8月4日}} * A repetition of the May festival to pray for good weather and agricultural prosperity. * **October** * *{{ill|Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭}}* (First Fruits Festival) – {{ill|October 18|ja|10月18日}}–{{ill|October 19|ja|10月19日}} * A festival where priests present freshly harvested grains as offerings to the gods. * **November** * *{{ill|Niinamesai|ja|新嘗祭}}* (New Harvest Festival) – {{ill|November 24|ja|11月24日}} * A festival in which the emperor offers the season’s first grains to the gods and partakes in them as an act of gratitude. * **December** * *{{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭}}* (Monthly Festival) – {{ill|December 18|ja|12月18日}}–{{ill|December 19|ja|12月19日}} === {{ill|Shikinen Sengu|ja|式年遷宮}} === [[File:Sengu of Tsukiyomi no Miya, August 2014.jpg|thumb|{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮}} ahead of {{ill|Ritchūsai|ja|立柱祭}} (photo taken on August 11, 2014) The shrine at the time is on the left, and the shrine under construction is on the right.]]The festivals and dates of the 62nd annual {{ill|Shikinen Sengu|ja|式年遷宮}} of the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮}} are as follows{{Cite web|和書|url=http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2259/|title=伊勢神宮外宮別宮のもう一つの「月の神様」もお引っ越し―残すは風宮|publisher=[[伊勢志摩経済新聞]]|date=2015-03-03|accessdate=2015-03-07|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150307142246/http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2259/|archivedate=2015-03-07}}{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.isejingu.or.jp/sikinen_2.html|title=月讀宮以下12別宮の遷宮 - 伊勢神宮|publisher=神宮司庁|accessdate=2015-03-07|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150210061619/http://www.isejingu.or.jp/sikinen_2.html|archivedate=2015-02-10}}。 ==== 2014 ==== * {{ill|August 20|ja|8月20日}} - {{ill|Ritchūsai|ja|立柱祭}}（りっちゅうさい）・{{ill|Jōtōsai|ja|上棟祭}}（じょうとうさい） * {{ill|October 5|ja|10月5日}} - {{ill|Nokitsukesai|ja|檐付祭}}（のきつけさい） * {{ill|November 5|ja|11月5日}} - {{ill|Irakasai|ja|甍祭}}（いらかさい） ==== 2015 ==== * {{ill|February 26|ja|2月26日}} - {{ill|Mitosai|ja|御戸祭}}（みとさい）・{{ill|Mifunashiro Hōnō-shiki|ja|御船代奉納式}}（みふなしろほうのうしき）・{{ill|Araikiyome|ja|洗清}}（あらいきよめ） * {{ill|February 27|ja|2月27日}} - {{ill|Kotsukisai|ja|杵築祭}}（こつきさい）・{{ill|Gochinsai|ja|後鎮祭}}（ごちんさい）・{{ill|Kawahara Ōharai|ja|川原大祓}}（かわらおおはらい） * {{ill|February 28|ja|2月28日}} - {{ill|Okazari|ja|御飾}}（おかざり）・{{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御}}（せんぎょ） * {{ill|March 1|ja|3月1日}} - {{ill|Ōmike|ja|大御饌}}（おおみけ）・{{ill|Hōhei|ja|奉幣}} Above, the {{ill|Ritchūsai|ja|立柱祭}}, {{ill|Jōtōsai|ja|上棟祭}}, {{ill|Kotsukisai|ja|杵築祭}}, {{ill|Gochinsai|ja|後鎮祭}}, {{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御}}, and {{ill|Hōhei|ja|奉幣}} were scheduled according to the divine decision (*{{ill|Gojijō|ja|御治定}}*) of the reigning emperor。 Additionally, on {{ill|February 22|ja|2月22日}}, the *{{ill|Oshiraishi-mochi|ja|お白石持}}* ceremony took place, during which approximately 1,000 participants from the {{ill|Miyago Hōkendan|ja|宮後奉献団}} carried sacred stones (*{{ill|Oshiraishi|ja|御白石}}*) in a cart from the {{ill|Urakuchi Intersection|ja|浦口交差点}} to {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月夜見宮}}, covering a distance of 1.2 km{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.chunichi.co.jp/article/mie/20150223/CK2015022302000028.html|title=次代につなぐ「エンヤ」 伊勢・月夜見宮でお白石持行事|author=中平雄大|publisher=[[中日新聞]]|date=2015-02-23|accessdate=2015-03-08|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150307161058/http://www.chunichi.co.jp/article/mie/20150223/CK2015022302000028.html|archivedate=2015-03-07}}。 This marked the completion of the *Oshiraishi-mochi* ceremonies for all auxiliary shrines (*{{ill|Betsugū|ja|別宮}}*)。 == Shrine Grounds (境内) == * **Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (月夜見宮)** - A **Betsugū** (auxiliary shrine) of {{ill|Toyouke Daijingu|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyouke Daijingu|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮}} (Outer Shrine of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|伊勢神宮}}). The shrine’s **architecture follows Shinmei-zukuri** and features **chigi (forked finials) cut horizontally** and **five katsuogi (short decorative logs)**, **a thatched roof**, and **a south-facing orientation**. - **Shikinen Sengu (式年遷宮)**: The shrine is **reconstructed every 20 years** according to the ancient practice of **Shikinen Sengu**. The **former shrine grounds** (古殿地, kodenchi) are located directly to the east and west of the current shrine. - **Traditional Legend**: It is said that in the past, when the people of **Miyago Town** were carrying **sacred timber (役木, yakugi)** for shrine reconstruction, they **passed through Yokaichiba Town**. At that moment, **a fire broke out in Miyago Town**, and the timber carriers **rushed back to extinguish it**. As a result, the people of Yokaichiba took over the role of **carrying the sacred timber**. Since then, in the **Okihikizome-shiki (御木曳初式, First Timber-Carrying Ceremony)**, **the people of Yokaichiba** have traditionally taken on the **honor of bringing the sacred timber to Tsukiyomi-no-Miya**. * **{{ill|Takagawara Shrine|ja|高河原神社|comment=no clue what happened there}}** - Dedicated to **Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto no Mitama (月夜見尊御魂, Spirit of Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto)**. Though located within **Tsukiyomi-no-Miya**, it is actually **a Sessha (摂社, auxiliary shrine) of Toyouke Daijingu (Outer Shrine).** * **{{ill|Inari Shrine|ja|稲荷社}}** – A shrine dedicated to **Inari**, the deity of **prosperity and agriculture**. * **Shukueya (宿衛屋)** – A **guardhouse** for shrine officials. --- == Kamiji Street (神路通り) == [[File:Kamiji Street from Tsukiyomi no Miya.jpg|thumb|Kamiji Street]] A **narrow, 4-meter-wide straight path** connects the **North Gate (北御門, Kita-mikado) of the Outer Shrine** to **Tsukiyomi-no-Miya**. This road is known as **"Kamiji Street" (神路通り, Kamiji-dōri), meaning "Path of the Gods,"** as it is **believed to be the route taken by deities.** See {{ill|Kamiji Street|ja|神路通り}} for details. --- == Worshipers' Association (信者団体) == In **1960 (Shōwa 35)**, a group of **Ise City residents** founded the **Tsukiyomi-kō (月夜見講)**, which was later renamed the **Tsukiyomi-no-Miya Hōsankai (月夜見宮奉賛会, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya Worshipers' Association).** - This organization **holds annual thanksgiving festivals** on **April 19 and September 19**, among other activities. --- == Access (交通) == * **Train:** - **10-minute walk** from **{{ill|Ise City Station|ja|伊勢市駅}}** (served by **JR {{ill|Sangu Line|ja|参宮線}}** & **Kintetsu {{ill|Yamada Line|ja|近鉄山田線}}**). - **5-minute walk** from the **North Gate of the Outer Shrine** via **Kamiji Street**. * **Bus:** - **3-minute walk** from **Shindō Bus Stop** (**{{ill|Mie Kotsu|ja|三重交通}} Bus**). - **Tsukiyomi-no-Miya-mae Bus Stop** (served by the **{{ill|Ise City Community Bus|ja|伊勢市コミュニティバス}}**). - Note: From **July 20, 2013**, the **Sangu Bus** operated by Mie Kotsu stopped at **Tsukiyomi-no-Miya-mae**, but this service was **discontinued on March 31, 2015**. * **Car:** - **Approx. 3 km** from **{{ill|Ise Interchange|ja|伊勢インターチェンジ}} (Ise Expressway).** - **Parking:** There are **only 2-4 parking spaces in front of the torii gate**, but **metered parking** is available on the south side of the street. --- [[Category:Shinto shrines in Japan]] [[Category:Ise Grand Shrine]] [[Category:Translated pages]] [[ja:月夜見宮]] == 脚注 == {{Reflist}} == 参考文献 == * 『月夜見宮参拝のしおり』（発行：神宮司庁） * 『お伊勢さんを歩こう』（発行：伊勢神宮崇敬会） * 『お伊勢まいり』（発行：伊勢神宮崇敬会） * 『宇治山田市史』 * 金子延夫『玉城町史 二巻 －南伊勢の歴史と伝承－』三重県郷土資料叢書第91集、三重県郷土資料刊行会、昭和58年12月10日 * 出版事業本部 国内情報部 第三編集部 編『[[るるぶ]] お伊勢まいり』るるぶ情報版近畿21、通巻4615号、[[JTBパブリッシング]]、2014年5月1日、92p.
