月夜見尊荒御魂 |社格 = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}}（小）
{{ill|Toyōke Daijingū|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyōke Daijingū|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyōke Daijingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyōke Daijingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}別宮 |創建 = [[延長 (元号)|延長]]5th year （[[927]]）以前 |本殿 = [[神明造]] |例祭= |地図 = {{location map|Japan Mie|lat_deg=34|lat_min=29|lat_sec=34.7|lon_deg=136|lon_min=42|lon_sec=21.3|label=月夜見宮|position=top|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|34|29|34.7|N|136|42|21.3|E}}}} |location = {{ill|Ise|WD=Q328067|1=Ise, Mie}} |coordinates = {{Coord|34.492972|N|136.705917|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} |deity = {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|WD=Q595520|1=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto}} |architecture_style = {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|WD=Q930545|1=Shinmei-zukuri}} }} '''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya''' (月夜見宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in Miyago, Ise City, Mie Prefecture辰巳出版（2013）：16ページ. It is a [[:en:Betsugū|Betsugū]] of [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]] {{ill|Toyōke Daijingū|ja|豊受大神宮|1=Toyōke Daijingū|2=ja|3=豊受大神宮|4=zh|5=豐受大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyōke Daijingū|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyōke Daijingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Outer Shrine)伊勢文化舎 編（2008）：39ページみらい出版（2013）：64ページ学研パブリッシング（2013）：69ページJTBパブリッシング（2011）：42ページ出版事業本部 国内情報部 第三編集部 編（2014）：34ページ三橋（2013）：124ページ。 It is a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|lt=Shikinaisha}}. == Overview == [[File:Tsukiyomi-nomiya(Geku)_00.JPG|thumb|300px|right|Aerial view of Tsukiyomi-no-Miya]] Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is an auxiliary shrine (betsugu) of the Outer Shrine (Geku), located about 300 meters north of Geku and approximately 500 meters west of {{ill|Iseshi Station|en|Iseshi Station|WD=Q6079748|lt=Ise City Station|1=Iseshi Station}}. It enshrines two deities within the same shrine building: {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto|ja|月夜見尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ツクヨミ|1=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q595520}} (Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto) and his fierce spirit, '''Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto-no-Aramitama''' (荒御魂 of Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto) . Unlike the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naikū)|ja|月讀宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naikū)|qq=}} auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine (Naiku), where Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto and his Aramitama are enshrined separately, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya uniquely houses both deities within a single structure . The only other auxiliary shrines that enshrine two deities in one building are {{ill|Kaze-no-Miya|ja|風宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kaze-no-Miya|qq=}} (Kaze-no-Miya) of the Outer Shrine and {{ill|Kazahinomi-no-Miya|ja|風日祈宮|lt=Kazahi-no-Miya|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazahinomi-no-Miya|qq=}} of the Inner Shrine, both enshrining Shinatsuhiko-no-Mikoto (級長津彦命) and Shinatsuhime-no-Mikoto (級長戸辺命). Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is the only auxiliary shrine of the Outer Shrine located outside the main precincts . Despite being in the urban area of Ise City, its grounds maintain a serene atmosphere . The moat surrounding three sides of the precinct is thought to be a remnant of a tributary of the {{ill|Miya River (Mie)|en|Miya River (Mie)|WD=Q6884164|lt=Miyagawa River (Mie Prefecture)|1=Miya River (Mie)}} . The {{ill|Mie Prefectural Route 37|ja|三重県道37号鳥羽松阪線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Route 37|1=Mie Prefectural Road Route 37|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11357923}} runs along the northern side of the moat and serves as the route for the '''Hatsuhobiki''' (初穂曳), a festival procession held every October in conjunction with the {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|en|Kannamesai Festival|WD=Q11255045|lt=Kannamesai|1=Kannamesai Festival}}. During this event, decorated carts carry the first harvested rice offerings to the Outer Shrine. Adjacent to the right rear of the shrine building is the auxiliary shrine of {{ill|Takagawara Shrine|ja|高河原神社|comment=no clue what happened there|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takagawara Shrine|qq=}} . To the left rear stands an {{ill|Inari shrine|ja|稲荷|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inari shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 稲荷神|1=Inari Ōkami|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q719665}} , and to the right is a large sacred camphor tree (大楠), where many people offer prayers . Like other auxiliary shrines outside the main precincts, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya has a '''Shukueiya''' (宿衛屋), a guardhouse where Shinto priests are present during visiting hours to distribute amulets, offer kagura performances, and manage food offerings (御饌). == Worshipped Deities (Saijin) == {{see also|{{ill|Saijin|ja|祭神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saijin|qq=}}}} * {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|en|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|WD=Q595520|WD=Q595520|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|1=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto}}（つきよみのみこと） * {{nihongo|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto-no-Ara-Mitama|月夜見尊荒御魂}} : {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|ja|月夜見尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ツクヨミ}} is the same deity as {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|ja|月讀尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ツクヨミ}}, the enshrined deity of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|ja|月讀宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|qq=}}, an auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine (Naikū) of {{ill|Ise Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|WD=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine|1=Ise Grand Shrine}}. He is the brother of {{ill|Amaterasu|en|Amaterasu|WD=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|1=Amaterasu}}. Since agricultural activities historically relied on the lunar calendar ({{ill|Lunar calendar|en|Lunar calendar|WD=Q185688|lt=Lunisolar calendar|1=Lunar calendar}}), he has been worshipped as a deity of agriculture. Additionally, he is also considered a river deity of {{ill|Takagawara|ja|高河原|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takagawara|1=Q23998361|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q23998361}} and a deity associated with women. According to the *{{ill|Jinmyō Hisho|ja|神名秘書|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jinmyō Hisho|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}*, his {{ill|Shintai|en|Shintai|WD=Q327532|lt=Shintai|1=Shintai}} (sacred object) is a {{ill|Mirror|en|Mirror|WD=Q35197|lt=mirror|1=Mirror}}. == Festivals == The shrine follows a festival schedule similar to that of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōtai Jingū|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, with offerings from the {{ill|Imperial House of Japan|en|Imperial House of Japan|WD=Q909452|lt=Imperial House of Japan|1=Imperial House of Japan}} during prayers for the harvest (*{{ill|Kinen-sai|en|Kinen-sai|WD=Q118906710|lt=Kinensai|1=Kinensai}}*), seasonal festivals (*{{ill|Tsukinamisai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinamisai|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=}}*), and major thanksgiving ceremonies (*{{ill|Kannamesai Festival|en|Kannamesai Festival|WD=Q11255045|lt=Kannamesai|1=Kannamesai Festival}}* and *{{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|en|Niiname-no-Matsuri|WD=Q11501518|lt=Niinamesai|1=Niiname-no-Matsuri}}*). * '''January''' **{{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Saitan-sai|qq=}}* (New Year's Festival) – {{ill|January 1|en|January 1|WD=Q2150|lt=January 1|1=January 1}} *** A festival celebrating the new year and praying for the eternal prosperity of the imperial lineage. **{{ill|Genshi-sai|ja|元始祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Genshi-sai|qq=}}* (Imperial Foundation Festival) – {{ill|January 3|en|January 3|WD=Q2156|lt=January 3|1=January 3}} *** A festival celebrating the origins of the imperial rule. * '''February''' **{{ill|Kenkoku Kinen-sai|ja|建国記念祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kenkoku Kinen-sai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}* (National Foundation Festival) – {{ill|February 11|en|February 11|WD=Q2335|lt=February 11|1=February 11}} *** Celebrating the founding of Japan by {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|en|Emperor Jimmu|WD=Q200188|lt=Emperor Jimmu|1=Emperor Jimmu}}. **{{ill|Kinen-sai|en|Kinen-sai|WD=Q118906710|lt=Kinensai|1=Kinensai}}* (Prayer Festival) – {{ill|February 18|en|February 18|WD=Q2343|lt=February 18|1=February 18}} *** A ceremony held early in the year to pray for abundant grain harvests and national peace. **{{ill|Tenchō-sai|ja|天長祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenchō-sai|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天皇誕生日|1=The Emperor's Birthday|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q72318}}* (Emperor’s Birthday Festival) – {{ill|February 23|en|February 23|WD=Q2352|lt=February 23|1=February 23}} *** A festival honoring the birthday of {{ill|Emperor Naruhito|ja|徳仁天皇|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Naruhito|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 徳仁|1=Naruhito|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q217096}}. * '''May''' **{{ill|Kazahinomi-sai|ja|風日祈祭|1=Kazahi-no-Misai|2=ja|3=風日祈祭|WD=Q135524493|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazahinomi-sai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135524493}}* (Wind and Sun Festival) – {{ill|May 14|en|May 14|WD=Q2561|lt=May 14|1=May 14}} *** Offerings are made at the Outer Shrine, Inner Shrine, and affiliated shrines to pray for protection from storms and a bountiful harvest. * '''June''' **{{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-sai|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=}}* (Monthly Festival) – {{ill|June 18|en|June 18|WD=Q2670|lt=June 18|1=June 18}}–{{ill|June 19|en|June 19|WD=Q2669|lt=June 19|1=June 19}} *** A biannual festival held in June and December to pray for the well-being of the nation and the emperor. Together with *{{ill|Kannamesai Festival|en|Kannamesai Festival|WD=Q11255045|lt=Kannamesai|1=Kannamesai Festival}}*, these are called the *Three Great Festivals* (三節祭 or 三時祭). * '''August''' **{{ill|Kazahinomi-sai|ja|風日祈祭|1=Kazahi-no-Misai|2=ja|3=風日祈祭|WD=Q135524493|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazahinomi-sai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135524493}}* (Wind and Sun Festival) – {{ill|August 4|en|August 4|WD=Q2784|lt=August 4|1=August 4}} *** A repetition of the May festival to pray for good weather and agricultural prosperity. * '''October''' **{{ill|Kannamesai Festival|en|Kannamesai Festival|WD=Q11255045|lt=Kannamesai|1=Kannamesai Festival}}* (First Fruits Festival) – {{ill|October 18|en|October 18|WD=Q2964|lt=October 18|1=October 18}}–{{ill|October 19|en|October 19|WD=Q2961|lt=October 19|1=October 19}} *** A festival where priests present freshly harvested grains as offerings to the gods. * '''November''' **{{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|en|Niiname-no-Matsuri|WD=Q11501518|lt=Niinamesai|1=Niiname-no-Matsuri}}* (New Harvest Festival) – {{ill|November 24|en|November 24|WD=Q3022|lt=November 24|1=November 24}} *** A festival in which the emperor offers the season’s first grains to the gods and partakes in them as an act of gratitude. * '''December''' **{{ill|Tsukinami-sai|ja|月次祭|1=Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-sai|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qq=}}* (Monthly Festival) – {{ill|December 18|en|December The shrine’s '''architecture follows Shinmei-zukuri''' and features '''chigi (forked finials) cut horizontally''' and '''five katsuogi (short decorative logs)''', '''a thatched roof''', and '''a south-facing orientation'''. ** '''Shikinen Sengu (式年遷宮)''': The shrine is '''reconstructed every 20 years''' according to the ancient practice of '''Shikinen Sengu'''. The '''former shrine grounds''' (古殿地, kodenchi) are located directly to the east and west of the current shrine. ** '''Traditional Legend''': It is said that in the past, when the people of '''Miyago Town''' were carrying '''sacred timber (役木, yakugi)''' for shrine reconstruction, they '''passed through Yokaichiba Town'''. At that moment, '''a fire broke out in Miyago Town''', and the timber carriers '''rushed back to extinguish it'''. As a result, the people of Yokaichiba took over the role of '''carrying the sacred timber'''. Since then, in the '''Okihikizome-shiki (御木曳初式, First Timber-Carrying Ceremony)''', '''the people of Yokaichiba''' have traditionally taken on the '''honor of bringing the sacred timber to Tsukiyomi-no-Miya'''. * '''{{ill|Takagawara Shrine|ja|高河原神社|comment=no clue what happened there|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takagawara Shrine|qq=}}''' - Dedicated to '''Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto no Mitama (月夜見尊御魂, Spirit of Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto)'''. Though located within '''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya''', it is actually '''a Sessha (摂社, auxiliary shrine) of Toyōke Daijingū (Outer Shrine).''' * '''{{ill|Inari Shrine|ja|稲荷社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inari Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 稲荷神社|1=Inari shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q514480}}''' – A shrine dedicated to '''Inari''', the deity of '''prosperity and agriculture'''. * '''Shukueya (宿衛屋)''' – A '''guardhouse''' for shrine officials. --- == Kamiji Street (神路通り) == [[File:Kamiji Street from Tsukiyomi no Miya.jpg|thumb|Kamiji Street]] }} {{translated page|ja|月夜見宮|qq=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|qq=ja|qq=月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya|version=99549095|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| {{Commons category|Tsukiyomi-no-miya (Geku)}} == AUTOGENERATED CONTENT FROM WIKIDATA == [[Category:Pages with duplicated content]] '''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku) (Q11516023)''' is a shrine in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is a betsugu (auxiliary shrine) of the Outer Shrine (Gekū), {{ill|lt=Toyouke Daijingu|Q11633343|WD=Q11633343|1=Toyōke Daijingū}}, of the {{ill|lt=Ise Grand Shrine|Q687168|WD=Q687168|1=Ise Grand Shrine}} complex.Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p. 16Ise Bunkasha, ed. (2008): p. 39Mirai Publishing (2013): p. 64Gakken Publishing (2013): p. 69JTB Publishing (2011): p. 42Publishing Business Headquarters, Domestic Information Dept., Third Editorial Dept., ed. (2014): p. 34Mitsuhashi (2013): p. 124 It is also a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shikinaisha|1=Shikinaisha|WD=Q134917286}}. === Enshrined deities === {{ill|WD=Q595520|lt=Tsukuyomi|Q595520|WD=Q595520|lt=**Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto**|1=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto}} (つきよみのみこと) **{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Aramitama of Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto|1=UNKNOWN}}** (つきよみのみことのあらみたま) :Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto is the same deity as Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto, who is enshrined at Tsukiyomi-no-miya (月讀宮), a betsugu of the Inner Shrine (Naikū). He is also said to be the younger brother of {{ill|lt=Amaterasu|Q455602|WD=Q455602|1=Amaterasu}}. Because people historically planned farm work using a lunar calendar ({{ill|lt=lunar calendar|Q185688|WD=Q185688|1=Lunar calendar}}) based on the waxing and waning of the moon, he has been regarded as a deity connected with agriculture. He is also considered a river deity of Takagawara and a deity connected with women as well. In *Shinmei Hisho*, the sacred object ({{ill|lt=shintai|Q327532|WD=Q327532|1=Shintai}}) is described as a {{ill|lt=mirror|Q35197|WD=Q35197|1=Mirror}}. === Overview === [[File:Tsukiyomi-nomiya(Geku)_00.JPG|thumb|300px|right|Tsukiyomi-no-miya seen from above]] Tsukiyomi-no-miya is a betsugu of the Outer Shrine located about 300 m north of the Gekū and about 500 m west of {{ill|lt=Ise-shi Station|Q6079748|WD=Q6079748|1=Iseshi Station}}. Two deities—{{ill|WD=Q595520|lt=Tsukuyomi|Q595520|WD=Q595520|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto|1=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto}} and his aramitama (rough/active spirit), **Aramitama of Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto**—are enshrined together in the same shrine building. At Tsukiyomi-no-miya (月讀宮), a betsugu of the Inner Shrine, Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto and his aramitama are enshrined in separate buildings, but at Tsukiyomi-no-miya (月夜見宮) they are enshrined together, which is a distinguishing feature. Other betsugu that enshrine two deities in a single building include {{ill|lt=Kaze-no-miya|Q11665463|WD=Q11665463|1=Kaze-no-Miya}} (an Outer Shrine betsugu) and {{ill|lt=Kaza-hi-no-miya|Q11665488|WD=Q11665488|1=Kazahinomi-no-Miya}} (an Inner Shrine betsugu), both of which enshrine Shinatsuhiko-no-Mikoto and Shinatobe-no-Mikoto. Among the Outer Shrine’s betsugu, this is the only shrine located outside the main sacred precinct (miyagi). Although it stands in the urban area of Ise, the grounds retain a quiet atmosphere. The moat surrounding three sides of the precinct is thought to be a remnant of a tributary of the {{ill|lt=Miyagawa River (Mie)|Q6884164|WD=Q6884164|1=Miya River (Mie)}}. {{ill|lt=Mie Prefectural Route 37 (Toba–Matsusaka Line)|Q11357923|WD=Q11357923|1=Mie Prefectural Road Route 37}}, which runs along the north side of the moat, becomes the venue for **{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Hatsuhiki|1=UNKNOWN}}** (the “Oise Grand Festival”) held each October in conjunction with the {{ill|lt=Kannamesai|Q11255045|WD=Q11255045|1=Kannamesai Festival}}, and the ceremonial carts carrying first fruits into the Outer Shrine pass through. The Outer Shrine’s sessha (subsidiary shrine), **{{ill|lt=Takagawara Shrine|Q17225931|WD=Q17225931|1=Takagawara Shrine}}**, is located behind the right side of the main shrine building. Behind the left side, an {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Inari|1=UNKNOWN}} is enshrined. To the right stands a large camphor tree, where some visitors offer prayers. As with other outlying betsugu, there is a **shukueiya** (a station where shrine staff stay during visiting hours), which distributes amulets and talismans and arranges kagura performances and offerings. === History === Its origins are not certain, but it is said that in ancient times it was called **Takagawara** and was a shrine that enshrined an agricultural deity. In the *Engishiki* compiled in 927 (the 5th year of Engi) during the reign of the 60th emperor, {{ill|lt=Emperor Daigo|Q329753|WD=Q329753|1=Emperor Daigo}}, it was ranked first among the Outer Shrine’s sessha. In the *Toyuke-no-miya Gishikichō* it is recorded as “Tsukuyomi Shrine,” in the *Engishiki Jinmyōchō* as “Tsukiyomi Shrine,” and in the *Ise Daijingū Shiki* as “Tsukiyomi Sha.” In 1210 (the 4th year of Jōgen), it was elevated to the status of a betsugu.Mitsuhashi (2013): p. 125 In the Meiji period, the Outer Shrine betsugu “tsukiyomi-no-miya” came to be written as **月夜見宮**, while the Inner Shrine betsugu “tsukiyomi-no-miya” came to be written as **月讀宮**. During the {{ill|lt=Ise riot|Q11379085|WD=Q11379085|1=Ise Riot}} of 1876 (Meiji 9), nearby towns burned, and because of concern that the fire might spread to Tsukiyomi-no-miya, the sacred object ({{ill|lt=shintai|Q327532|WD=Q327532|1=Shintai}}) was temporarily moved to {{ill|lt=Kaze-no-miya|Q11665463|WD=Q11665463|1=Kaze-no-Miya}}.Kaneko (1983): p. 214 During the {{ill|lt=Pacific War|Q184425|WD=Q184425|1=Pacific War}}, the {{ill|lt=Ujiyamada air raid|Q18990749|WD=Q18990749|1=Ujiyamada Air Raid}} occurred on July 29, 1945 (Shōwa 20). Although all surrounding houses burned down, due to desperate firefighting by the {{ill|lt=military|Q8473|WD=Q8473|1=Military}} and the fact that an incendiary bomb lodged in the thatched roof failed to explode, only the shrine buildings of Tsukiyomi-no-miya remained standing amid the ruins.Yano (2006): pp. 184–185 However, a contracted shukueiin (guard attendant) was killed in the air raid, and the miyatsukasa (shrine official) suffered severe burns.Yano (2006): p. 185 === Festivals === Rites comparable to those of the Inner Shrine are performed, and for the Kinensai, Tsukinamisai, Kannamesai, and Niinamesai, offerings ({{ill|lt=heihaku|Q11481885|WD=Q11481885|1=Hanpei}}) are presented from the {{ill|lt=Imperial Household|Q909452|WD=Q909452|1=Imperial House of Japan}}. * January ** Saitansai (New Year’s Day Festival) (January 1) A festival celebrating the New Year and praying for the eternal continuity of the imperial line. ** Genshisai (January 3) A festival celebrating the origin of the imperial succession at the start of the year. * February ** Kenkoku Kinen-sai (National Foundation Festival) (February 11) A festival celebrating the founding of the nation by {{ill|lt=Emperor Jimmu|Q200188|WD=Q200188|1=Emperor Jimmu}}. ** Kinensai (February 18) A festival held at the beginning of the year praying for abundant harvests and national peace. ** Tenchōsai (February 23) A festival celebrating the birthday of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Emperor Naruhito|1=UNKNOWN}}. * May ** Kazahinomisai (May 14) A rite in which offerings are presented not only at the Outer and Inner Shrines but also at betsugu, massha, and sessha, praying that there will be no damage from wind and rain and that the five grains will be abundant. * June ** Tsukinamisai (June 18–19) A festival held in June and December on the 11th, praying for national peace and the emperor’s well-being; at the Shrine it is also called one of the “Three Seasonal Festivals” together with the Kannamesai. * August ** Kazahinomisai (August 4) Same as above. * October ** {{ill|lt=Kannamesai|Q11255045|WD=Q11255045|1=Kannamesai Festival}} (October 18–19) A festival in which priests offer newly harvested grain as sacred food ({{ill|lt=shinsen|Q11591045|WD=Q11591045|lt=Ōmike|1=Shinsen}}). * November ** {{ill|lt=Niinamesai|Q11501518|WD=Q11501518|1=Niiname-no-Matsuri}} (November 24) A festival in which the emperor offers newly harvested grain to the gods, partakes of it himself, and gives thanks for the harvest. * December ** Tsukinamisai (December 18–19) === Shikinen sengū === [[File:Sengu of Tsukiyomi no Miya, August 2014.jpg|thumb|Tsukiyomi-no-miya before the Ritchūsai (photo taken August 11, 2014)
Left: the then-current shrine building; right: the shrine building under construction]] The ceremonies and schedule for the 62nd shikinen sengū of Tsukiyomi-no-miya are as follows:{{Cite web|ja|url=http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2259/|title=Another “moon deity” of Ise Grand Shrine’s Outer Shrine betsugu also moves—only Kaze-no-miya remains|publisher=Ise-Shima Keizai Shimbun|date=2015-03-03|accessdate=2015-03-07|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150307142246/http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2259/|archivedate=2015-03-07}}{{Cite web|ja|url=http://www.isejingu.or.jp/sikinen_2.html|title=Relocations of 12 betsugu including Tsukiyomi-no-miya - Ise Grand Shrine|publisher=Jingu Administration Office|accessdate=2015-03-07|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150210061619/http://www.isejingu.or.jp/sikinen_2.html|archivedate=2015-02-10}} **2014** * August 20 – Ritchūsai (Pillar-Raising Festival) / Jōtōsai (Ridgepole-Raising Festival) * October 5 – Nokitsukesai (Eaves-Attaching Festival) * November 5 – Irakasai (Roofing Festival) **2015** * February 26 – Mitosai / Mifunashiro Hōnōshiki / Araikiyome * February 27 – Kotsukisai / Gochinsai / Kawara Ōharae * February 28 – Okazari / Sengyo (Transfer of the deity) * March 1 – Ōmike / Hōhei Among these, the Ritchūsai, Jōtōsai, Kotsukisai, Gochinsai, Sengyo, and Hōhei are conducted according to dates determined by imperial decision. In addition, on February 22, 2015, the **Oshiraishi-mochi** event was held, in which about 1,000 people of the Miyago offering group pulled ceremonial carts loaded with sacred white stones for 1.2 km from the Uraguchi intersection to Tsukiyomi-no-miya.{{Cite web|ja|url=http://www.chunichi.co.jp/article/mie/20150223/CK2015022302000028.html|title=“Enya” linking to the next generation: Oshiraishi-mochi event at Tsukiyomi-no-miya in Ise|author=Yudai Nakahira|publisher=Chunichi Shimbun|date=2015-02-23|accessdate=2015-03-08|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150307161058/http://www.chunichi.co.jp/article/mie/20150223/CK2015022302000028.html|archivedate=2015-03-07}} With this, all oshiraishi-mochi events for the betsugu were completed. === Precincts === * Tsukiyomi-no-miya — A betsugu of the Outer Shrine (Gekū) of the Ise Grand Shrine complex. In keeping with the Outer Shrine, the thatched **shinmei-zukuri** building faces south and has outward-cut chigi and five (an odd number) katsuogi. The old site for relocation (kodenchi) lies adjacent to it east–west. As with the Outer Shrine, a relocation ({{ill|lt=Shikinen sengū|Q3959472|WD=Q3959472|1=Jingū Shikinen Sengū}}) is performed once every 20 years. There is a tradition that when people of Miyago pulled the “yakukan” (construction timber) and reached Yōkaichiba-chō, a fire broke out in Miyago, and the pullers returned to fight it; the people of Yōkaichiba-chō took over pulling the timber, and ever since, at the **{{ill|lt=Okihiki-zome-shiki|Q11489125|WD=Q11489125|1=Okihiki}}** the people of Yōkaichiba-chō have pulled and offered the timber to Tsukiyomi-no-miya. * {{ill|lt=Takagawara Shrine|Q17225931|WD=Q17225931|1=Takagawara Shrine}} — Enshrined deity: the mitama (spirit) of Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto. Located within the precincts of Tsukiyomi-no-miya, but it is a sessha of Toyouke Daijingu (the Outer Shrine) of Ise Grand Shrine. * {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Inari Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}} * Shukueiya === Kamiji Street === [[File:Kamiji Street from Tsukiyomi no Miya.jpg|thumb|Kamiji Street]] The straight road about 4 m wide running from the Outer Shrine’s Kita-mikado (North Gate) to Tsukiyomi-no-miya is regarded as “the road the gods pass,” and is called **Kamiji Street** (神路通り). See the article {{ill|lt=Kamiji Street|Q30114580|WD=Q30114580|1=Kamiji Street}}. === Devotee organization === In 1960 (Shōwa 35), a Tsukiyomi confraternity (Tsukiyomi-kō) was formed mainly by worshippers living in Ise, later renamed the Tsukiyomi-no-miya Hōsankai. The Hōsankai carries out activities such as holding a festival of gratitude for divine blessings on April 19 and September 19 each year. === Access === * About a 10-minute walk from {{ill|lt=Ise-shi Station|Q6079748|WD=Q6079748|1=Iseshi Station}} on the JR {{ill|lt=Sangū Line|Q872023|WD=Q872023|1=Sangū Line}} and the Kintetsu Yamada Line. * About a 5-minute walk from the Outer Shrine Kita-mikado entrance via {{ill|lt=Kamiji Street|Q30114580|WD=Q30114580|1=Kamiji Street}}.JTB Publishing (2011): p. 43 * About a 3-minute walk from the Shindō bus stop (Mie Kōtsū), and immediately from the “Tsukiyomi-no-miya-mae” stop on the Ise City community bus “Okage Bus.”From July 20, 2013, Mie Kōtsū’s “Sangū Bus” stopped at the “Tsukiyomi-no-miya-mae” stop, but as of March 31, 2015, service to that stop was discontinued. * About 3 km from the Ise Interchange on the {{ill|lt=Ise Expressway|Q6079578|WD=Q6079578|1=Ise Expressway}}. * Parking: Only 2–4 cars can park in front of the torii gate,
